definition_zh: 顾客满意；顾客满意度（顾客对产品或服务体验的总体评价）
definition_en: the degree to which customers are pleased with a product, service or transaction
core_image: 餐厅门口的意见卡上打满勾，用餐的客人带着笑离开，店员把卡片收进透明盒子
scene: 服务台前，几位顾客离店前填写评价卡，店员把卡片收进透明的收集箱。Customer satisfaction drives repeat visits more reliably than advertising.
sceneCN: 这里 customer satisfaction 指「顾客对整体体验的满意程度」（第 1 个义项：顾客对产品、服务与交易的整体评价）；句意为顾客满意比广告更能稳定地带来回头客。图中可辨识物件：评价卡、勾选栏、透明收集箱、离店顾客。

pos.zh: 顾客满意；顾客满意度（不可数；指不同顾客群体或多次测量时可作可数）
（作定语）用于衡量顾客满意的，如满意度调查、满意度评分等搭配

forms.label: 复数（少见，指不同群体或多次测量）

senses.title: Overall approval of an experience
senses.definition: the overall judgement that a product or service has met the buyer's expectations
senses.definitionCN: 顾客对产品或服务是否达到预期的总体判断
senses.example: Customer satisfaction rose after the hotel added late check-out.
senses.exampleCN: 酒店增加延迟退房服务后，顾客满意度上升。
senses.why: satisfaction is built from satis 'enough' plus facere 'to do', so the word asks whether enough has been done for the buyer.
senses.whyCN: satisfaction 由 satis「足够」加 facere「做」构成，因此这个词问的是卖方是否「做得够」。

senses.title: A score produced by a survey
senses.titleCN: 调查量出的满意度得分
senses.definition: a number reported after buyers rate their experience on a scale
senses.definitionCN: 顾客按量表打分后得出的数值
senses.example: The chain reports customer satisfaction every quarter as a percentage.
senses.exampleCN: 该连锁企业每季度以百分比形式公布顾客满意度。
senses.why: once satisfaction became a target, it needed a number, and the phrase took on the sense of a measured index.
senses.whyCN: 当满意成为管理目标，就需要一个数字，这个短语便有了「可测量的指数」义。

senses.title: Reaction to a single transaction
senses.definition: the immediate judgement formed during one purchase, visit or service encounter
senses.definitionCN: 在某一次购买、到访或服务接触中当场形成的判断
senses.example: Customer satisfaction at the counter depends heavily on the wait.
senses.exampleCN: 柜台前的顾客满意度在很大程度上取决于等候时间。
senses.why: customer marks the person at the point of sale, so the phrase can be read narrowly as what one buyer feels at that moment.
senses.whyCN: customer 指交易现场的那个人，所以这个短语也可窄读为一个买主在那一刻的感受。

senses.title: Satisfaction accumulated over years
senses.titleCN: 长期关系中累积的满意
senses.definition: the sum of many experiences with one supplier over months or years
senses.definitionCN: 数月或数年间与同一供应商多次打交道后累积下来的评价
senses.example: Customer satisfaction built over a decade can survive one bad delivery.
senses.exampleCN: 十年累积的顾客满意度能经受住一次糟糕的配送。
senses.why: firms speak of the phrase across a whole relationship because memory outlasts a single receipt.
senses.whyCN: 企业谈这个短语时覆盖整段关系，因为记忆比一张小票活得更久。

senses.title: Satisfaction as a driver of repeat business
senses.definition: the level of contentment that makes a buyer return instead of switching to a rival
senses.definitionCN: 使买主回头而不转投对手的满意程度
senses.example: Customer satisfaction predicts repurchase better than a discount does.
senses.exampleCN: 顾客满意度比折扣更能预测复购。
senses.why: marketers read satisfaction as a cause rather than a result once repeat purchase becomes the goal.
senses.whyCN: 一旦复购成为目标，营销者就把满意看作原因而非结果。

senses.title: A figure tracked as a management target
senses.titleCN: 作为考核指标跟踪的数字
senses.definition: a figure that managers set, track and reward as part of performance review
senses.definitionCN: 管理者设定、跟踪并据此考核的绩效数字
senses.example: Customer satisfaction is one of the three targets in the manager's bonus plan.
senses.exampleCN: 顾客满意度是经理奖金方案中的三项指标之一。
senses.why: the phrase becomes countable when it names a dashboard figure rather than a feeling.
senses.whyCN: 当这个短语指仪表盘上的数字而非一种感受时，它变得可数。

senses.title: Satisfaction after a complaint is handled
senses.definition: the judgement a buyer makes after a problem has been acknowledged and repaired
senses.definitionCN: 问题被承认并解决之后买主作出的评价
senses.example: Customer satisfaction recovered only after the airline refunded the ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 直到航空公司退还票款，顾客满意度才恢复。
senses.why: service research splits the phrase because a failure and its repair are judged separately from routine service.
senses.whyCN: 服务研究把这个短语单独切出，因为失误与修复是和日常服务分开评价的。

senses.title: Residents' approval of a public service
senses.titleCN: 居民对公共服务的满意
senses.definition: the same judgement applied by residents to a government service rather than a shop
senses.definitionCN: 居民对政府服务而非商店作出的同类判断
senses.example: Customer satisfaction with the water utility is now surveyed by the city.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府如今会调查居民对供水服务的满意度。
senses.why: the word customer widened to cover anyone served, even when no money changes hands.
senses.whyCN: customer 的词义扩大为任何被服务的人，即使没有金钱交易。

intro.en: Customer enters English through Anglo-French custumer, from custume 'habit, customary payment', itself from Latin consuetudo. Satisfaction is Latin satisfactio, from satis 'enough' and facere 'to do'. The two-word phrase is twentieth-century marketing vocabulary. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: customer 经盎格鲁-法语 custumer 进入英语，其源为 custume「习惯、惯常缴纳」，再上溯拉丁 consuetudo。satisfaction 来自拉丁 satisfactio，由 satis「足够」与 facere「做」构成。整个短语是 20 世纪营销词汇。年代均为约数。

items.en: Consuetudo 'custom, habit' was built from con- 'together' and suescere 'to become accustomed'. Its stem reached Old French as custume, the source of custom.
items.cn: consuetudo「习惯、惯例」由 con-「共同」与 suescere「变得习惯」构成；其词干进入古法语作 custume，即 custom 的来源。

items.en: Custumer named a person who had habitual dealings with a place, and in trade it came to mean one who buys regularly. The suffix -er marks the person, as in baker and buyer.
items.cn: custumer 指与某地常有往来的人，在商业中转而指经常购买的人；后缀 -er 标记人，如 baker、buyer。

items.en: Satis 'enough' plus facere 'to do, make' produced satisfacere 'to do enough, to discharge a claim'. The noun satisfactio first meant the settlement of a debt or an offence.
items.cn: satis「足够」加 facere「做、造」构成 satisfacere「做得够、清偿要求」；名词 satisfactio 最初指清偿债务或赎罪。

items.en: In English satisfaction kept its legal sense of settling a claim through the fourteenth century and only later, in the sixteenth, took the modern sense of contentment.
items.cn: 英语 satisfaction 在 14 世纪仍保留「清偿要求」的法律义，到 16 世纪才出现现代「满意」义。

items.en: Customer satisfaction became a fixed term with the growth of market research in the mid twentieth century, and later acquired the abbreviation CSAT in service management.
items.cn: 随着 20 世纪中期市场研究的兴起，customer satisfaction 成为固定术语，后来在服务管理中又得到缩写 CSAT。

items.en: No exact first citation for the full phrase is recorded; the earliest uses belong to mid twentieth-century marketing writing. The pre-Latin origin of suescere is a reconstruction, not a demonstrated form.
items.cn: 完整短语的最早书证没有确切记录，早期用例属 20 世纪中期的营销写作；suescere 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式，并非已证形式。

note.en: Group one holds neighbouring forms from the same Latin stock that are constantly swapped; group two holds words that describe a related state without measuring it.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词源、常被混用的邻近词形；第二组是描述相关状态却不作测量的词。

entries.definition: A blend of satisfy and suffice, coined in decision theory for accepting an adequate option instead of the best one; its second half is Latin sufficere, not facere.
entries.definitionCN: satisfy 与 suffice 的混成词，在决策理论中指接受「够用」的方案而非最优方案；它的后半来自拉丁 sufficere，而非 facere。

entries.definition: Built on the same satisfac- stem, it judges a thing as good enough rather than describing the buyer's feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 satisfac- 词干，但它评价事物「够好」，而非描述买主的感受。

entries.definition: From Latin satietas, also from satis 'enough', but it names physical fullness, especially after eating, not commercial approval.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 satietas，同样出自 satis「足够」，但指生理上的饱足，尤指吃饱，而非商业上的认可。

entries.definition: The plural of custom means duties charged on imported goods; it comes from the same habit-and-payment line but is not the buyer.
entries.definitionCN: custom 的复数指对进口货物征收的关税；它同出「习惯与缴纳」这条线，但并不指买主。

entries.definition: A quiet inner state of being satisfied with what one has; it is not measured, scored or tied to a purchase.
entries.definitionCN: 对现状感到满足的安静内心状态，不被测量、打分，也不与某次购买绑定。

entries.definition: The satisfaction of completing a promise or duty; it stresses delivery of an obligation, while customer satisfaction stresses the buyer's verdict.
entries.definitionCN: 完成承诺或职责后的满足，强调义务的兑现；顾客满意则强调买主的评判。

entries.definition: A formal or informal judgement that something is acceptable; it can be given without any feeling of pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 对某事可否接受的正式或非正式判定；它可以不含任何愉悦感受。

entries.definition: Continued support for a person or brand; satisfaction may cause it, but loyalty is behaviour over time rather than a rating.
entries.definitionCN: 对某人或某品牌的持续支持；满意可能促成忠诚，但忠诚是长期行为而非一个评分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: satis 'enough' + facere 'do': satisfaction is the sense that enough has been done.
normal.cn: satis「足够」+ facere「做」：满意就是觉得对方做得够。

normal.en: customer is the person who comes back by custom, so the phrase already carries the idea of repeat buying.
normal.cn: customer 是按惯例回来的那个人，因此这个短语本身已含重复购买之意。

normal.en: The family runs customer, custom, satisfy, satisfaction, satisfactory, satisfied, satisfying.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 customer、custom、satisfy、satisfaction、satisfactory、satisfied、satisfying。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the measured sense: satisfaction survey, satisfaction score, satisfaction rating.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出测量义：满意度调查、满意度评分、满意度评级。

normal.en: Service writing shortens it to CSAT, a three-letter index on a dashboard.
normal.cn: 服务管理写作把它缩写成 CSAT，即仪表盘上的三字母指标。

abstract.en: Picture a card with five boxes, four ticked and one left empty.
abstract.cn: 想象一张有五个方框的卡片，四个打了勾，一个空着。

abstract.en: Picture the same shopper returning to the same counter on the same weekday.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个顾客在同一个星期几回到同一个柜台。

abstract.en: Picture a glass box slowly filling with identical cards.
abstract.cn: 想象一个透明箱子慢慢被相同的卡片填满。

examples.en: The airline measures customer satisfaction after every long-haul flight.
examples.cn: 该航空公司在每次长途航班后测量顾客满意度。

examples.en: Customer satisfaction fell when the return window was cut to seven days.
examples.cn: 退货期限缩短到七天后，顾客满意度下降。

examples.en: A polite reply to a complaint can restore customer satisfaction within a day.
examples.cn: 对投诉作出礼貌回应，可以在一天内恢复顾客满意度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「customer（顾客）+ satisfaction（满足）」——顾客的要求被做得够，心里就满足 → 顾客满意度

root: customer 经古法语 custumer 上溯拉丁 consuetudo「习惯」（con- + suescere「变得习惯」）；satisfaction 来自拉丁 satisfactio（satis「足够」+ facere「做」）。整个短语是 20 世纪市场研究的产物。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one judgement: a buyer decides that enough has been done, and that judgement is then counted, timed, summed over years, turned into a target, applied to a repair, and finally extended to public services.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个判断展开：买主认定对方做得够，这个判断再被计数、被限定在单次、被多年累加、变成考核指标、用于补救，最后延伸到公共服务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a comment card full of ticks, dropped into a clear box by a customer on the way out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张打满勾的意见卡，被离店的顾客投进透明箱子。

branches.en: MET EXPECTATION: the plain state, and the same state summed over a long relationship.
branches.cn: 预期被满足：朴素状态，以及长期关系中被累加起来的同一状态。

branches.en: MEASURED AND MOMENTARY: a survey turns the feeling into a number, while a single counter visit keeps it momentary.
branches.cn: 被测量与即时的：调查把感受变成数字，单次柜台经历则让它停留在当下。

branches.en: CAUSE OF RETURN: satisfaction is read forward as a reason a buyer comes back.
branches.cn: 回头的原因：满意被向前读作买主回来的理由。

branches.en: TARGET AND WIDER SERVE: a dashboard figure, then the same figure applied to residents served by a city.
branches.cn: 指标与更广的服务：先是仪表盘数字，再是用于城市居民的同一种数字。

branches.en: AFTER FAILURE: a complaint and its repair are judged on their own.
branches.cn: 失误之后：投诉与补救被单独评价。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived noun for the buyer to a Latin noun for contentment; both halves carry suffixes that also build other common words.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源的「买主」名词接在拉丁来源的「满足」名词上；两部分所带的后缀还构成其他常用词。

latinIntro.en: Latin consuetudo supplies custom and customer, while satis and facere supply satisfy, satisfaction and satisfactory; satis also feeds satiety and satiate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 consuetudo 提供 custom 与 customer，satis 与 facere 提供 satisfy、satisfaction 与 satisfactory；satis 还衍生 satiety 与 satiate。

items.structure: Latin consuetudo via Old French custume
items.example: Custom decides which side of the road traffic uses.
items.exampleCN: 习惯决定车辆靠道路哪一侧行驶。

items.example: The customer asked for the same brand again.
items.exampleCN: 这位顾客又要了同一个品牌。

items.meaning: to meet a need or expectation
items.example: One small change satisfied most complaints.
items.exampleCN: 一处小改动就满足了大部分投诉。

items.example: Her satisfaction showed in a short nod.
items.exampleCN: 她轻轻点头，显出满意。

items.example: The repair was satisfactory but not elegant.
items.exampleCN: 修理结果合格，但算不上漂亮。

items.example: The diners left satisfied.
items.exampleCN: 食客们满意地离开。

items.example: It was a slow but satisfying meal.
items.exampleCN: 这顿饭上得慢，却令人满足。

items.example: Simon argued that managers satisfice rather than maximise.
items.exampleCN: 西蒙认为管理者会选择「够用」而非「最优」。

items.example: Rich food brings satiety quickly.
items.exampleCN: 油腻的食物很快带来饱足感。

items.example: The market showed an insatiable appetite for the device.
items.exampleCN: 市场对这款设备表现出无法满足的需求。

definition_zh: 品牌忠诚；品牌忠诚度（消费者持续偏好并重复选择某一品牌）
definition_en: the tendency of customers to keep choosing one brand over its rivals
core_image: 同一位顾客的购物车里，同一款标志的包装一次次出现，货架上其他品牌积了薄灰
scene: 货架前，一位顾客第三次拿起同一款麦片，旁边几个品牌的包装还蒙着薄灰。Brand loyalty keeps that cereal in the same kitchen year after year.
sceneCN: 这里 brand loyalty 指「消费者对某一品牌的持续偏好与重复选择」（第 1 个义项：顾客长期优先选择同一品牌）；句意为品牌忠诚让那款麦片年年出现在同一间厨房里。图中可辨识物件：重复出现的同款包装、邻架积灰的竞品、购物车、厨房储物柜。

pos.zh: 品牌忠诚；品牌忠诚度（不可数；指不同品牌或不同群体的忠诚时可作可数）

forms.label: 复数（少见，指对不同品牌的忠诚）

derivatives.zh: 品牌塑造；品牌形象设计

senses.title: Habitual preference for one brand
senses.titleCN: 对某一品牌的习惯性偏好
senses.definition: the tendency to favour one brand consistently when several acceptable options exist
senses.definitionCN: 在存在多个可接受选项时，持续偏向同一品牌的倾向
senses.example: Brand loyalty kept the older detergent on the shelf long after rivals improved.
senses.exampleCN: 对手产品早已改进，品牌忠诚仍让那款旧洗衣液留在货架上。
senses.why: brand began as a burned mark of ownership, and loyalty as lawful faithfulness, so the phrase fuses a mark with fidelity.
senses.whyCN: brand 原指烙上的所有权标记，loyalty 原指守法的忠实，因此这个短语把「标记」与「忠实」合在一起。

senses.title: Repeat purchase behaviour
senses.definition: the observable pattern of buying the same brand again and again
senses.definitionCN: 可以观察到的、反复购买同一品牌的行为模式
senses.example: Brand loyalty shows up in the scanner data as a flat repeat-purchase line.
senses.exampleCN: 品牌忠诚在收银扫描数据中表现为一条平稳的复购线。
senses.why: researchers split loyalty into what people do and what they feel; this sense covers only the doing.
senses.whyCN: 研究者把忠诚分为「做什么」与「感觉什么」，这个义项只覆盖「做什么」。

senses.title: Trust and emotional attachment
senses.definition: a favourable attitude and sense of trust that makes a buyer prefer the brand even when a rival is cheaper
senses.definitionCN: 使买主在对手更便宜时仍偏好该品牌的正面态度与信任感
senses.example: Brand loyalty here means refusing the cheaper jar without reading the label.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的品牌忠诚指不看标签就拒绝更便宜的那一罐。
senses.why: loyalty originally described faithfulness owed to a sovereign, and that emotional colour survives in this sense.
senses.whyCN: loyalty 原指臣民对君主的忠实，这层情感色彩在这个义项里留存下来。

senses.title: A measured loyalty rate
senses.definition: a figure such as repurchase rate or share of wallet used to compare brands
senses.definitionCN: 用于比较品牌的复购率、钱包份额等数值
senses.example: The report put brand loyalty at sixty per cent of repeat buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把品牌忠诚度定为复购买主中的六成。
senses.why: once loyalty became a marketing target, it was turned into a rate that can be reported alongside sales.
senses.whyCN: 当忠诚成为营销目标，它就被转成可与销售额并列汇报的比率。

senses.title: Lock-in created by switching costs
senses.definition: continued buying caused by the cost or effort of changing suppliers rather than by preference
senses.definitionCN: 因更换供应商的成本或麻烦而非偏好造成的持续购买
senses.example: Brand loyalty in printer ink is mostly lock-in, since the cartridges fit only one machine.
senses.exampleCN: 打印机墨盒的品牌忠诚多半是锁定，因为墨盒只配一种机器。
senses.why: the phrase can name behaviour without affection, and economists mark that case as switching cost.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以指不含感情的行为，经济学家把这种情况标为转换成本。

senses.title: Identity expressed through a brand community
senses.titleCN: 通过品牌社群表达身份
senses.definition: loyalty that comes from belonging to a group of users and using the brand to signal identity
senses.definitionCN: 来自用户群体归属感、并以品牌标示身份的忠诚
senses.example: Brand loyalty among the club members looks more like team support than shopping.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部成员之间的品牌忠诚更像是支持球队，而非购物。
senses.why: brands became badges once mass production made products hard to tell apart, so loyalty could express identity.
senses.whyCN: 大规模生产使产品难以区分之后，品牌成了徽章，忠诚便可表达身份。

senses.title: Specified brands in business buying
senses.titleCN: 企业采购中的品牌指定
senses.definition: a purchasing rule that names an approved brand so that buyers cannot substitute another
senses.definitionCN: 规定只能采购指定品牌、买主不得替换的采购规则
senses.example: Brand loyalty in the hospital contract was written into the specification list.
senses.exampleCN: 医院合同中的品牌忠诚被写进了规格清单。
senses.why: in institutional buying the preference is codified, so the phrase shifts from a feeling to a clause.
senses.whyCN: 在机构采购中，偏好被写成条文，于是这个短语从感受变成了条款。

senses.title: Trust in a source label
senses.titleCN: 对来源标记的信任（比喻义）
senses.definition: the same stickiness applied to a media outlet, party or institution treated as a brand
senses.definitionCN: 把媒体、政党或机构当作品牌后所表现出的同一种黏性
senses.example: Brand loyalty to the newspaper survived two ownership changes.
senses.exampleCN: 读者对这份报纸的品牌忠诚经受住了两次换主。
senses.why: the word brand widened beyond goods, and loyalty followed it into politics and media.
senses.whyCN: brand 的词义越出商品，loyalty 也跟着它进入政治与媒体领域。

intro.en: Brand is Old English brand 'firebrand, burning piece', from a Germanic root for burning; its commercial sense grew out of marks burned on cattle and casks. Loyalty comes from Old French loialte, from Latin legalis 'of the law', from lex 'law'. The phrase is twentieth-century marketing language. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: brand 是古英语 brand「火把、燃烧的木片」，出自表示「燃烧」的日耳曼词根；其商业义由烙在牲畜与木桶上的标记发展而来。loyalty 来自古法语 loialte，上溯拉丁 legalis「法律的」，再上溯 lex「法律」。整个短语是 20 世纪营销用语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Brand meant a piece of burning wood, and the related verb bærnan meant to burn. A mark burned into hide or wood showed who owned the animal or the cask.
items.cn: brand 指一块燃烧的木头，相关动词 bærnan 意为「燃烧」。烙进兽皮或木桶的印记标明牲畜或木桶归谁所有。

items.en: By the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries brand named the mark itself, and in the nineteenth it shifted to the commercial identity behind the mark.
items.cn: 到 17、18 世纪，brand 指印记本身；19 世纪又转指标记背后的商业身份。

items.en: Lex 'law' produced legalis 'of the law', which passed through Old French as loial 'lawful, faithful' and then as the noun loialte.
items.cn: lex「法律」构成 legalis「法律的」，经古法语作 loial「守法的、忠实的」，再构成名词 loialte。

items.en: Loyalty first meant lawful and faithful conduct toward a ruler or lord; the transfer to customers is a modern extension of that older fidelity.
items.cn: loyalty 最初指对君主或领主的守法与忠实行为；用于顾客是现代对这层旧忠实的延伸。

items.en: Brand loyalty became a standard term in market research in the mid twentieth century, as panel data made repeat buying visible.
items.cn: 20 世纪中期，随着面板数据使重复购买变得可见，brand loyalty 成为市场研究的标准术语。

items.en: The exact first printed use of the full phrase is not recorded; early examples come from mid twentieth-century advertising and research writing. The deeper Germanic origin of brand is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 完整短语的最早印刷用例没有记录，早期例子出自 20 世纪中期的广告与研究写作；brand 更早的日耳曼来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same two words but with different grammatical jobs, plus one unrelated look-alike; group two holds near neighbours that describe attachment without the commercial setting.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这两个词、但语法作用不同的词形，外加一个无关的形近词；第二组是描述依附关系、但不带商业场景的近义词。

entries.definition: The gerund of brand, naming the work of designing and maintaining a commercial identity; it can exist without any loyal customers.
entries.definitionCN: brand 的动名词，指设计与维护商业身份的工作；它可以完全没有忠实顾客而存在。

entries.definition: The financial value attached to a brand name; loyalty is one input into it, but equity is measured in money.
entries.definitionCN: 附着在品牌名称上的财务价值；忠诚是它的一个输入，但品牌资产以金钱计量。

entries.definition: From Dutch brandewijn 'burnt wine', a distilled spirit; it looks like brand but shares none of its history.
entries.definitionCN: 来自荷兰语 brandewijn「烧过的酒」，指蒸馏酒；它形似 brand，却与 brand 没有词源关系。

entries.definition: A person who stays faithful to a ruler, cause or group; the noun marks a person where loyalty marks a tendency.
entries.definitionCN: 对君主、事业或群体保持忠实的人；这个名词指人，而 loyalty 指倾向。

entries.definition: Attachment to a supplier regardless of whether it has a recognizable brand; brand loyalty narrows the object to a name and its marks.
entries.definitionCN: 对某供应商的依附，不论其是否有可识别的品牌；品牌忠诚把对象收窄为一个名称及其标记。

entries.definition: The share of customers who stay over a period; it is the measurable outcome that loyalty is supposed to produce.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间内留下来的顾客比例；它是忠诚理应产生的可测结果。

entries.definition: A conscious promise to support someone or something; commitment can be declared, while loyalty is often habitual and unspoken.
entries.definitionCN: 有意识地承诺支持某人或某事；承诺可以被宣告，而忠诚常是习惯性的、未说出口的。

entries.definition: A repeated behaviour that has become automatic; habit explains how loyalty persists, but it carries no promise of fidelity.
entries.definitionCN: 已变得自动的重复行为；习惯解释了忠诚如何维持，却不含忠实的承诺。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: brand is a burned mark, loyalty is faithfulness: the phrase is a mark that people stay faithful to.
normal.cn: brand 是烙上的印记，loyalty 是忠实：这个短语就是人们对其保持忠实的那个印记。

normal.en: The family runs brand, branding, branded, loyal, loyally, loyalist, disloyal.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 brand、branding、branded、loyal、loyally、loyalist、disloyal。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the commercial sense: brand loyalty programme, brand loyalty survey, brand loyalty index.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出商业义：品牌忠诚计划、品牌忠诚调查、品牌忠诚指数。

normal.en: Loyalty is measured two ways: what buyers do (repeat purchase) and what they feel (trust).
normal.cn: 忠诚有两种测法：买主做了什么（重复购买）与买主感觉到什么（信任）。

normal.en: Its opposite is brand switching, the movement from one label to another.
normal.cn: 它的反面是品牌转换，即从一个牌子转向另一个牌子。

abstract.en: Picture a shopping list where the same brand name is written in the same handwriting for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一张购物清单，同一个品牌名用同一种笔迹写了好多年。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf where one box is handled daily and the rest gather dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一个货架，一盒每天被拿起，其余的都积了灰。

abstract.en: Picture a football scarf worn for the same club through a losing season.
abstract.cn: 想象一条球迷围巾，在输球的赛季里仍为同一支球队戴着。

examples.en: Brand loyalty kept the family buying the same tea for three generations.
examples.cn: 品牌忠诚让这家人三代都买同一款茶。

examples.en: A single recall can wipe out years of brand loyalty.
examples.cn: 一次召回就可能抹掉多年积累的品牌忠诚。

examples.en: The loyalty programme rewards repeat buyers but does not create brand loyalty by itself.
examples.cn: 忠诚计划奖励复购买主，但本身并不创造品牌忠诚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「brand（烙印/品牌）+ loyalty（忠诚）」——认准那个烙印，一直买它 → 品牌忠诚

root: brand 为古英语 brand「燃烧的木片」，商业义由烙在牲畜与木桶上的所有权标记发展而来；loyalty 经古法语 loialte 上溯拉丁 legalis「法律的」（lex「法律」）。整个短语为 20 世纪营销用语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one fidelity: a buyer keeps choosing a marked source, and that fidelity is then observed as behaviour, felt as trust, counted as a rate, explained as lock-in, expressed as identity, written into contracts, and finally transferred to media and politics.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种忠实展开：买主持续选择一个有标记的来源，这份忠实再被当作行为观察、当作信任感受、当作比率计量、解释为锁定、表达为身份、写进合同，最后转移到媒体与政治。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a burned mark on a cask that tells a buyer, year after year, which one to reach for.
core.cn: 核心意象：木桶上烙下的印记，年复一年告诉买主该拿哪一个。

branches.en: PREFERENCE AND TRUST: the plain attachment, then the same attachment felt as confidence.
branches.cn: 偏好与信任：朴素的依附，以及同一依附被感受为信心。

branches.en: BEHAVIOUR SEEN FROM OUTSIDE: repeat purchase is loyalty as a scanner can record it.
branches.cn: 从外部看到的行为：重复购买是扫描器能记录的忠诚。

branches.en: COUNTED AND EXPLAINED: a rate in a report, then a cost that keeps buyers in place without affection.
branches.cn: 被计量与被解释：报告里的比率，以及不含感情却把买主留在原地的成本。

branches.en: IDENTITY AND CONTRACT: a badge worn by a community, and a brand named in a purchasing rule.
branches.cn: 身份与合同：社群佩戴的徽章，以及采购规则中指定的品牌。

branches.en: BEYOND GOODS: the same fidelity given to a newspaper or a party.
branches.cn: 越出商品：同一种忠实被给予报纸或政党。

intro.en: The phrase pairs a Germanic noun of burning and marking with a Latin-derived noun of lawful faithfulness; the two halves bring their own suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个短语把日耳曼来源的「燃烧与标记」名词，与拉丁来源的「守法忠实」名词配在一起；两部分各带自己的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin lex and legalis supply loyal, loyalty and disloyal; the Germanic brand supplies brand, branding, branded and unbranded.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lex 与 legalis 提供 loyal、loyalty 与 disloyal；日耳曼来源的 brand 提供 brand、branding、branded 与 unbranded。

items.meaning: a mark of ownership; a commercial identity
items.example: The brand was stamped on every crate.
items.exampleCN: 每个木箱上都打上了这个品牌。

items.meaning: the work of building a commercial identity
items.example: The branding changed, but the recipe did not.
items.exampleCN: 品牌形象变了，配方却没变。

items.example: Branded goods cost more than loose ones.
items.exampleCN: 带品牌的商品比散装贵。

items.example: The unbranded tin tasted the same.
items.exampleCN: 无品牌的那罐味道一样。

items.structure: Old French loial, from Latin legalis
items.meaning: faithful to a person or cause
items.example: A loyal reader renews without being asked.
items.exampleCN: 忠实的读者不用提醒就会续订。

items.example: Loyalty outlasted the founder.
items.exampleCN: 这份忠诚比创始人活得还久。

items.example: She loyally bought the same paper for decades.
items.exampleCN: 她几十年忠实地买同一份报纸。

items.example: The loyalists stayed with the club after relegation.
items.exampleCN: 球队降级后，忠实拥护者仍留在俱乐部。

items.example: A disloyal supplier sold the design to a rival.
items.exampleCN: 一家不忠的供应商把设计卖给了对手。

items.meaning: the money value of a brand name
items.example: Brand equity rose after the redesign.
items.exampleCN: 重新设计后，品牌资产上升。

definition_zh: 竞争者；竞争对手；参赛者
definition_en: a person, firm or team that competes with another for the same customers, prize or resource
core_image: 两条跑道并排，两个人影在同一终点线前加速，观众只看谁先到
scene: 赛道边，两辆赛车并排冲过弯道，维修区里的人盯着计时屏。A smaller competitor undercut the leader by cutting its delivery times.
sceneCN: 这里 competitor 指「在同一市场中争夺顾客的对手」（第 1 个义项：与企业争夺同一批顾客的另一家企业）；句意为一家规模较小的竞争者通过缩短交货时间压过了领先者。图中可辨识物件：并排的两辆赛车、计时屏、维修区、终点线。

pos.zh: 竞争者；竞争对手；参赛者

senses.title: A firm chasing the same customers
senses.titleCN: 争夺同一批顾客的企业
senses.definition: a business that sells goods or services to the same buyers as another business
senses.definitionCN: 与另一家企业面向同一批买主出售商品或服务的企业
senses.example: The two competitors cut prices within a week of each other.
senses.exampleCN: 两家竞争对手在一周之内先后降价。
senses.why: the Latin verb meant 'to seek together', so a competitor is literally one who seeks the same thing alongside others.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「一起寻求」，因此 competitor 字面上就是与他人一起寻求同一样东西的人。

senses.title: An athlete or team in a contest
senses.definition: a person or team taking part in a sporting or academic contest
senses.definitionCN: 参加体育或学术比赛的选手或队伍
senses.example: She beat three competitors to win the regional final.
senses.exampleCN: 她击败三名参赛者，赢得地区决赛。
senses.why: sport kept the oldest sense: people striving for one prize on the same field.
senses.whyCN: 体育保留了最古老的义项：在同一场地上争夺同一个奖赏的人。

senses.title: A rival for a post or place
senses.titleCN: 竞聘职位或名额的对手
senses.definition: a person who applies for the same job, school place or grant
senses.definitionCN: 申请同一职位、学位名额或资助的人
senses.example: Six competitors were shortlisted for the post.
senses.exampleCN: 有六名竞争者进入了该职位的候选名单。
senses.why: the same 'seeking together' structure applies whenever a limited number of places is on offer.
senses.whyCN: 只要名额有限，「一起寻求」的结构就同样适用。

senses.title: A substitute product or technology
senses.definition: a product or technology that can take the place of another in the buyer's use
senses.definitionCN: 在买主的使用中能取代另一产品的产品或技术
senses.example: Rail travel is a competitor to short-haul flights.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路出行是短途航班的竞争者。
senses.why: economists widened the term because a rival need not sell the same thing, only serve the same need.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家扩大了这个词的用法，因为对手不必卖同样的东西，只需满足同样的需求。

senses.title: A species rival in ecology
senses.titleCN: 生态学中争夺资源的物种
senses.definition: an organism that uses the same limited resource as another species or individual
senses.definitionCN: 与另一物种或个体使用同一种有限资源的生物
senses.example: The two bird species are competitors for the same nesting holes.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种鸟是同一批筑巢洞的竞争者。
senses.why: ecology borrowed the market word because both describe a scramble for a fixed supply.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用了市场用语，因为两者都描述对固定供给的争夺。

senses.title: An atom-like firm in a market model
senses.titleCN: 市场模型中的原子式厂商
senses.definition: one of many small sellers in a model where no single one can affect price
senses.definitionCN: 在没有任何单一卖方能影响价格的模型中，众多小卖方之一
senses.example: In perfect competition no competitor can move the market price alone.
senses.exampleCN: 在完全竞争中，没有哪个竞争者能单独左右市场价格。
senses.why: the economics textbook makes the competitor small by definition, so the word loses its sense of threat.
senses.whyCN: 经济学教科书按定义把竞争者设得很小，于是这个词失去了威胁意味。

senses.title: A potential entrant not yet selling
senses.titleCN: 尚未开卖但可能进入的对手
senses.definition: a firm that could enter the market and constrain incumbents even before it does
senses.definitionCN: 可能进入市场、甚至在进入前就约束现有企业的企业
senses.example: A new entrant can be a competitor before it opens a single store.
senses.exampleCN: 新进入者在开第一家店之前就已是竞争者。
senses.why: antitrust counts potential entry because the threat of a competitor can discipline prices.
senses.whyCN: 反垄断把潜在进入计入，因为竞争者的威胁就能约束价格。

senses.title: Any party seeking the same scarce thing
senses.titleCN: 任何争夺同一稀缺资源的方
senses.definition: a person, group or institution pursuing the same limited fund, attention or territory
senses.definitionCN: 追逐同一有限资金、注意力或领地的人、群体或机构
senses.example: Two charities became competitors for the same donation pool.
senses.exampleCN: 两家慈善机构成了同一笔捐款池的竞争者。
senses.why: the word generalizes once 'seeking together' is detached from shops and prizes.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「一起寻求」脱离商店与奖赏，这个词就一般化了。

intro.en: Competitor is Latin competitor 'one who strives with another', from competere, built on com- 'together' and petere 'to seek, aim at'. Petere also gives petition and appetite. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: competitor 来自拉丁 competitor「与他人相争的人」，其动词 competere 由 com-「共同」与 petere「寻求、瞄准」构成。petere 还衍生 petition 与 appetite。年代均为约数。

items.en: Petere meant 'to seek, head for, attack'. Petition and appetite descend from the same verb, one asking and one reaching for food.
items.cn: petere 意为「寻求、前往、攻击」。petition 与 appetite 都出自同一动词，一个表示请求，一个表示对食物的欲求。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus petere produced competere 'to seek together, strive jointly', and in legal use 'to claim jointly'.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 petere 构成 competere「一起寻求、共同力争」，在法律用语中指「共同主张」。

items.en: The noun competitor named the person who strives alongside another for the same object; English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 competitor 指与他人为同一目标相争的人；英语在 16 世纪借入。

items.en: Competere also meant 'to be fit or proper for', which produced competent and competence; that branch shares the verb but not the rivalry.
items.cn: competere 还表示「适合、相称」，由此产生 competent 与 competence；这一支共享动词，却不含相争之义。

items.en: From the nineteenth century competitor became a standard word for a firm in a market, and competition law gave it a technical edge.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，competitor 成为市场中企业的标准称法，竞争法又赋予它技术性含义。

items.en: The exact first English citation is approximate. The deeper origin of petere is reconstructed rather than demonstrated.
items.cn: 最早的英语书证年代只是约数。petere 的更深来源属重构形式，并非已证形式。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin verb that are easy to confuse with the rival noun; group two holds near synonyms for the person or side one is up against.
note.cn: 第一组是同出那个拉丁动词、易与「对手」名词混淆的词；第二组是表示「所面对的人或一方」的近义词。

entries.definition: The activity or event of competing; a competitor is a participant, while competition is what they take part in.
entries.definitionCN: 竞争这一活动或赛事；competitor 是参与者，competition 是他们参与的那件事。

entries.definition: Describing a person, price or market that is able to compete; it qualifies the contest rather than naming a rival.
entries.definitionCN: 形容有能力竞争的人、价格或市场；它修饰竞争，而非指称对手。

entries.definition: From the 'be fit for' branch of competere, meaning capable or legally qualified; it has nothing to do with rivalry.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 competere 的「适合」一支，意为有能力或法律上合格的；与相争无关。

entries.definition: One who presents a petition, from petere 'seek'; a petitioner seeks a decision, not a customer.
entries.definitionCN: 提交请愿书的人，出自 petere「寻求」；请愿者寻求的是裁决，不是顾客。

entries.definition: From Latin rivalis, one who draws water from the same stream; it stresses a continuing contest between two sides.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 rivalis，指同一条溪流取水的人；强调双方持续相争的关系。

entries.definition: The person or team on the other side of a contest; it fits sport and debate better than markets.
entries.definitionCN: 比赛或辩论中站在对面的人或队伍；比用于市场更贴合体育与辩论。

entries.definition: An opponent seen as an enemy; it adds hostility that competitor, a neutral market word, does not carry.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为敌人的对手；它增添了敌意，而中性的 market 用词 competitor 并不带这层意思。

entries.definition: A person or firm that enters a market or contest; an entrant becomes a competitor once it actually takes part.
entries.definitionCN: 进入市场或比赛的个人或企业；进入者真正参与后才成为竞争者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: com- 'together' + petere 'seek': one who seeks the same thing alongside you.
normal.cn: com-「共同」+ petere「寻求」：与你一起寻求同一样东西的人。

normal.en: The family runs compete, competition, competitive, competitiveness, competing, competitor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 compete、competition、competitive、competitiveness、competing、competitor。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the market sense: main competitor, direct competitor, competitor analysis.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出市场义：主要对手、直接对手、对手分析。

normal.en: Competent looks like a twin but came from the 'be fit for' branch of the same verb.
normal.cn: competent 看似同出一源，却来自同一动词的「适合」一支。

normal.en: Sports writing uses the same word for a runner, a team or a chess player.
normal.cn: 体育写作也用同一个词指跑者、队伍或棋手。

abstract.en: Picture two runners reaching for the same ribbon at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两名跑者在同一瞬间伸手去抓同一条终点带。

abstract.en: Picture two shops on one street watching each other's price tags.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条街上的两家店互相盯着对方的价签。

abstract.en: Picture two birds inspecting the same hole in a tree.
abstract.cn: 想象两只鸟查看着树上的同一个洞。

examples.en: The incumbent lost a third of its share to a foreign competitor.
examples.cn: 原有企业把三分之一的市场份额丢给了一家外国竞争者。

examples.cn: 对手的失败可能与它的成功一样危险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「com（共同）+ pet（追求）+ itor（人）」——一起追求同一块蛋糕的人 → 竞争者

root: 拉丁 competere「一起寻求、共同力争」= com-「共同」+ petere「寻求、瞄准」；competitor 为拉丁名词「与他人在同一目标上相争的人」。petere 另衍生 petition 与 appetite。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of seeking: someone aims at the same object as another, and that aim is then seen in a shop, on a track, at a job interview, in a substitute product, in a habitat, in an economic model, before entry, and in any scramble for a scarce thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「寻求」动作展开：某人与另一人瞄准同一目标，这个瞄准再依次出现在商店、跑道、求职、替代产品、栖息地、经济模型、进入之前，以及任何对稀缺物的争夺中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two runners side by side, both reaching for one ribbon.
core.cn: 核心意象：两名跑者并排，同伸一只手去抓同一条终点带。

branches.en: MARKET AND SUBSTITUTE: the firm chasing the same buyer, and the product that serves the same need.
branches.cn: 市场与替代：追逐同一买主的企业，以及满足同一需求的产品。

branches.en: PEOPLE IN CONTESTS: a runner on a track and an applicant on a shortlist.
branches.cn: 竞赛中的人：跑道上的选手与候选名单上的申请者。

branches.en: SPECIES IN A HABITAT: the same scramble transposed to nesting holes.
branches.cn: 栖息地中的物种：同一种争夺被移用到筑巢洞上。

branches.en: MODEL AND THREAT: an atom in a textbook market, and a firm that has not entered yet.
branches.cn: 模型与威胁：教科书市场里的原子，以及尚未进入的企业。

branches.en: ANY SCARCE PRIZE: charities, parties or families seeking one limited pool.
branches.cn: 任何稀缺奖赏：慈善机构、政党或家庭争夺同一个有限资源池。

intro.en: Competitor is a Latin noun whose verb is still productive in English, so the whole family can be read from com-, petere and the agent suffix.
intro.cn: competitor 是一个拉丁名词，其动词在英语中仍能产，因此整个词族可从 com-、petere 与施事后缀读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin petere supplies compete, competition, competitor and petition; com- marks the shared aim, and -or marks the person.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 petere 提供 compete、competition、competitor 与 petition；com- 标记共同目标，-or 标记人。

items.example: A competent driver checks the mirror first.

latinEntries.meaning: to strive together; to be fit for

definition_en: the ability of a firm, industry or country to sell its goods and services against rivals
core_image: 一张赛跑成绩表上，同一个选手的排名年年前移，旁边的训练记录越写越厚
scene: 工厂的装配线旁，主管把本月成本表与对手的报价单并排贴在墙上。Rising competitiveness in the region forced every plant to retool.
sceneCN: 这里 competitiveness 指「企业或地区相对对手的竞争能力」（第 1 个义项：企业在市场上胜过对手的能力）；句意为该地区竞争力的上升迫使每座工厂更新设备。图中可辨识物件：成本表、对手报价单、装配线、并排对比的墙面。

senses.title: A firm's ability to beat rivals
senses.definition: the capacity of one business to win customers and sales against its rivals
senses.definitionCN: 一家企业在与对手争夺顾客与销量时取胜的能力
senses.example: The firm's competitiveness rests on faster delivery rather than lower wages.
senses.exampleCN: 这家企业的竞争力靠的是更快的交货，而非更低的工资。
senses.why: competitive plus -ness turns an adjective of striving into the noun for the capacity itself.
senses.whyCN: competitive 加 -ness，把表示「相争」的形容词变成表示这种能力本身的名词。

senses.title: A country's export strength
senses.definition: the ability of a national economy to sell abroad and attract investment
senses.definitionCN: 一国经济在海外销售并吸引投资的能力
senses.example: The country's export competitiveness improved after the currency was adjusted.
senses.exampleCN: 汇率调整后，该国的出口竞争力有所提升。
senses.why: governments borrowed the firm-level word and scaled it up to whole economies.
senses.whyCN: 政府借用了企业层面的词，并把它放大到整个经济体。

senses.title: The strength of a cluster or region
senses.titleCN: 产业集群或区域的实力
senses.definition: the collective ability of linked firms in one place to outperform firms elsewhere
senses.definitionCN: 同一地点相互关联的企业整体胜过外地企业的能力
senses.example: The cluster's competitiveness attracted suppliers from three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这个产业集群的竞争力吸引了三国的供应商。
senses.why: the unit can be a place rather than a company, because linked firms share suppliers and skills.
senses.whyCN: 计量单位可以是地点而非公司，因为相互关联的企业共享供应商与技能。

senses.title: Cost and price competitiveness
senses.definition: the ability to offer similar goods at a lower cost or price than rivals
senses.definitionCN: 以低于对手的成本或价格提供同类商品的能力
senses.example: Cheap energy gave the mills a cost competitiveness that lasted a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价能源给了这些工厂持续十年的成本竞争力。
senses.why: the phrase is often narrowed to price because the cheapest offer is the easiest advantage to measure.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法常被收窄到价格，因为最便宜的报价是最容易测量的优势。

senses.title: Strength built on productivity and innovation
senses.titleCN: 由生产率与创新支撑的竞争力
senses.definition: long-run competitive strength created by efficiency gains and new products rather than by cheap inputs
senses.definitionCN: 由效率提升与新产品而非廉价投入创造的长期竞争实力
senses.example: Innovation, not wage cuts, sustains long-run competitiveness.
senses.exampleCN: 维系长期竞争力的是创新，而非削减工资。
senses.why: economists separate this sense because cost advantage can vanish when prices or wages change.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把这一义项单列，因为成本优势会随价格或工资变化而消失。

senses.title: Advantage from exchange rates and wages
senses.titleCN: 汇率与工资带来的优势
senses.definition: a temporary edge produced by currency movements or lower labour costs
senses.definitionCN: 由汇率变动或较低劳动成本造成的暂时优势
senses.example: A strong currency hurt the sector's competitiveness overnight.
senses.exampleCN: 本币走强一夜之间削弱了该行业的竞争力。
senses.why: in trade policy the word often names price effects that no firm controls.
senses.whyCN: 在贸易政策中，这个词常指企业无法左右的价格效应。

senses.title: A rank on a competitiveness index
senses.definition: a position in a published ranking that compares economies or industries
senses.definitionCN: 在比较经济体或产业的公开排名中的位置
senses.example: The economy moved up ten places in the competitiveness index.
senses.exampleCN: 该经济体在竞争力指数上上升了十位。
senses.why: once the concept was indexed, the noun came to mean a score as well as a capacity.
senses.whyCN: 当这一概念被编成指数，这个名词也指分数，而不只是能力。

senses.title: Relative strength in any contest
senses.titleCN: 任何争夺中的相对实力
senses.definition: the degree to which any side can hold its own against competitors
senses.definitionCN: 任何一方在与对手相争时能站稳的程度
senses.example: Both teams trained for months, and their competitiveness showed in the final.
senses.exampleCN: 两队都训练了数月，决赛里显出了各自的竞争力。
senses.why: detached from trade, the noun simply measures how well a side can fight for a share.
senses.whyCN: 脱离贸易语境后，这个名词只衡量一方争夺份额的实力。

intro.en: Competitiveness is an English-built noun: the Latin verb competere gives competitive through -ive, and the native suffix -ness turns that adjective into a quality. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: competitiveness 是英语自造的名词：拉丁动词 competere 经 -ive 构成 competitive，本族后缀 -ness 再把形容词变成性质名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Competere 'to seek together, strive jointly' joins com- 'together' to petere 'seek'. The rivalry sense was fixed in Latin before English borrowed it.
items.cn: competere「一起寻求、共同力争」把 com-「共同」接在 petere「寻求」上；相争义在英语借入前已在拉丁语中固定。

items.en: The suffix -ivus formed adjectives of tendency, as in competitivus; French -if and English -ive continue that pattern.
items.cn: 后缀 -ivus 构成表示倾向的形容词，如 competitivus；法语 -if 与英语 -ive 延续了这一模式。

items.en: Competitive entered English in the seventeenth century as an adjective for things able to contend, and later for prices and markets.
items.cn: competitive 在 17 世纪进入英语，形容能够相争的事物，后来也用于价格与市场。

items.en: The native suffix -nes, now -ness, turned adjectives into nouns of quality, as in darkness and readiness; competitiveness is a regular formation.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -nes（今 -ness）把形容词变成性质名词，如 darkness、readiness；competitiveness 是规则的构成。

items.en: Competitiveness became a policy term in the late twentieth century, when reports began ranking nations and regions by it.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，随着报告开始据此给国家与地区排名，competitiveness 成为政策术语。

items.en: The exact first use of the noun is not recorded; nineteenth-century economics already used competitive in the modern sense. No step in the word chain is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词的最早用例没有确切记录；19 世纪经济学已在使用现代义的 competitive。词形链条各环节并无存疑之处。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same verb that answer a different question; group two holds related measures of performance that are not the same as the capacity itself.
note.cn: 第一组是同出那个动词、却回答不同问题的词；第二组是相关的绩效指标，与「能力」本身并不等同。

entries.definition: The process or event of rivals striving; competitiveness is a capacity, while competition is the struggle in which it shows.
entries.definitionCN: 对手相争的过程或赛事；competitiveness 是一种能力，competition 是这种能力得以显现的斗争。

entries.tag: a skill, not a market edge
entries.definition: From the 'be fit for' branch of competere: a specific skill or qualification a person or firm possesses.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 competere 的「适合」一支：人或企业具备的具体技能或资格。

entries.definition: The adjective that competitiveness nominalises; it describes the side or price, not the abstract capacity.
entries.definitionCN: competitiveness 所名词化的形容词；它描述一方或价格，而非抽象能力。

entries.definition: The active participle, used for sides currently in the contest or for mutually exclusive claims.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，用于当前正在相争的各方，或相互排斥的主张。

entries.definition: The ratio of output to input in production; it is a source of competitiveness, not the same as the ability to sell.
entries.definitionCN: 生产中产出与投入的比率；它是竞争力的来源，但不等同于销售能力。

entries.definition: The use of the least resources for a result; a firm can be efficient yet fail to sell if demand is weak.
entries.definitionCN: 用最少资源取得结果；企业可以很高效，却在需求疲弱时卖不出去。

entries.definition: One favourable condition; competitiveness is the overall capacity that such conditions support.
entries.definitionCN: 某一项有利条件；competitiveness 是这些条件所支撑的总体能力。

entries.definition: How well a firm actually did in a period; it reports results, while competitiveness predicts what results are possible.
entries.definitionCN: 企业在一段时间内的实际表现；它汇报结果，而竞争力预测可能取得什么结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: competitive + -ness: the quality of being able to strive.
normal.cn: competitive + -ness：能够相争的性质。

normal.en: The family runs compete, competition, competitor, competitive, competitively, competitiveness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 compete、competition、competitor、competitive、competitively、competitiveness。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the policy sense: international competitiveness, cost competitiveness, competitiveness index.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出政策义：国际竞争力、成本竞争力、竞争力指数。

normal.en: The word can be measured at three levels: firm, industry, country.
normal.cn: 这个词可在三个层面计量：企业、产业、国家。

normal.en: Its usual sources are productivity, innovation, skills and infrastructure.
normal.cn: 它的常见来源是生产率、创新、技能与基础设施。

abstract.en: Picture a rankings board where one name climbs a line each year.
abstract.cn: 想象一张排名板，同一个名字每年往上爬一行。

abstract.en: Picture a training log that grows thicker while the race times grow shorter.
abstract.cn: 想象训练记录越写越厚，而比赛用时越来越短。

abstract.en: Picture two factories on one river, one retooling while the other stands still.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条河边的两座工厂，一座在换设备，另一座原地不动。

examples.en: The report ranked the economy by competitiveness rather than by income.
examples.cn: 该报告按竞争力而非收入给经济体排名。

examples.en: Firms that ignore training slowly lose competitiveness.
examples.cn: 忽视培训的企业会慢慢失去竞争力。

examples.en: Currency swings can change competitiveness before any factory adjusts.
examples.cn: 汇率波动能在任何工厂作出调整之前改变竞争力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「competitive（竞争）+ ness（性质）」——能在赛场上争一争的性质 → 竞争力

root: 拉丁 competere「一起寻求、共同力争」（com- + petere「寻求」）→ 拉丁 -ivus 构成 competitivus → 英语 competitive + 本族后缀 -ness。整词为英语自造的性质名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one capacity: a side can hold its own, and that capacity is then scaled from a firm to a country and a region, narrowed to costs, traced to productivity, tied to exchange rates, turned into a rank, and finally applied to any contest.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种能力展开：一方能站稳脚跟，这种能力再从事企业放大到国家与区域、收窄到成本、追溯到生产率、联系到汇率、变成排名，最后用于任何竞赛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a training log that thickens while the race times shorten.
core.cn: 核心意象：训练记录越写越厚，比赛用时越来越短。

branches.en: THE FIRM: the plain capacity of one business to win sales.
branches.cn: 企业：一家企业赢得销量的朴素能力。

branches.en: SCALED UP: the same capacity attributed to an economy or to a linked cluster.
branches.cn: 被放大：同一种能力被归给一个经济体或一个关联集群。

branches.en: PRICE AND CURRENCY: the cheapest offer, and the exchange-rate edge no firm controls.
branches.cn: 价格与汇率：最便宜的报价，以及企业无法左右的汇率优势。

branches.en: THE DURABLE BASE: productivity and innovation keep the capacity from evaporating.
branches.cn: 持久的基础：生产率与创新使这种能力不致蒸发。

branches.en: SCORE AND ANY CONTEST: a published rank, then the same capacity in a race or a debate.
branches.cn: 分数与任何竞赛：公开排名，以及赛跑或辩论中的同一种能力。

intro.en: The noun stacks a Latin verb, a Latin adjective suffix and a native English suffix, so each layer can be read separately.
intro.cn: 这个名词叠了一个拉丁动词、一个拉丁形容词后缀与一个英语本族后缀，因此每一层都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin competere gives compete and competition, -ivus gives competitive, and Old English -nes gives competitiveness.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 competere 提供 compete 与 competition，-ivus 提供 competitive，古英语 -nes 提供 competitiveness。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把相争收束为共同的竞赛。

items.example: Both sides seek the same buyer.
items.exampleCN: 双方寻求同一个买主。

items.example: Small shops compete on service.

items.example: The price is competitive in the region.
items.exampleCN: 这个价格在本地区有竞争力。

items.example: The tickets were priced competitively.
items.exampleCN: 票价定得有竞争力。

items.meaning: the quality of being able to compete
items.example: The index tracks national competitiveness.
items.exampleCN: 该指数跟踪国家竞争力。

items.example: A rival opened across the street.
items.exampleCN: 街对面开了一家竞争对手。

items.example: Competition keeps margins thin.
items.exampleCN: 竞争使利润空间变薄。

items.example: The old mill became uncompetitive.
items.exampleCN: 这座老厂失去了竞争力。

items.example: The role lists five core competencies.
items.exampleCN: 该岗位列出五项核心能力。

latinEntries.meaning: to strive together; to be fit for

definition_en: a condition or resource that lets a firm outperform its rivals in a market
core_image: 同一场比赛里，一名选手脚下多了一双带钉的跑鞋，起跑线却没有变
scene: 两家工厂的成品并排摆在展台上，其中一家的产品更薄、更省电，价签却相同。A durable competitive advantage usually rests on resources rivals cannot copy.
sceneCN: 这里 competitive advantage 指「企业胜过对手的有利条件」（第 1 个义项：使企业在市场中表现优于对手的条件或资源）；句意为持久的竞争优势通常建立在对手无法复制的资源上。图中可辨识物件：并排展台、更薄更省电的产品、相同价签、对手的产品。

senses.title: A general edge over rivals
senses.definition: any condition that lets a firm serve buyers better or more cheaply than its rivals
senses.definitionCN: 使企业比对手更好或更便宜地服务买主的任何条件
senses.example: A reliable supply chain gave the retailer a competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 可靠的供应链给了这家零售商竞争优势。
senses.why: advantage comes from avant 'before', so the phrase names a position ahead of rivals rather than a fixed property.
senses.whyCN: advantage 来自 avant「在前」，因此这个短语指相对对手靠前的位置，而非固定属性。

senses.title: Cost advantage
senses.definition: the ability to produce or deliver at a lower cost than competitors
senses.definitionCN: 以低于竞争对手的成本生产或交付的能力
senses.example: Low labour costs were its original competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 低劳动成本是它最初的竞争优势。
senses.why: cost is the easiest edge to measure, so the phrase often takes this narrow reading in industry reports.
senses.whyCN: 成本是最容易测量的优势，因此在产业报告中这个短语常取这一窄义。

senses.title: Differentiation advantage
senses.definition: an edge from offering something buyers value that rivals do not offer
senses.definitionCN: 通过提供买主看重而对手不提供的东西取得的优势
senses.example: Design became the brand's competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 设计成了这个品牌的竞争优势。
senses.why: when price cannot be lowered further, the edge must come from a difference buyers are willing to pay for.
senses.whyCN: 当价格无法再降，优势就只能来自买主愿意为之付费的差异。

senses.title: A durable advantage
senses.definition: an edge that survives imitation and market change for a long period
senses.definitionCN: 长期经受住模仿与市场变化的优势
senses.example: A patent-protected process is a sustainable competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 受专利保护的工艺是一种可持续的竞争优势。
senses.why: strategy writing added durable because most edges are copied quickly and stop being advantages.
senses.whyCN: 战略写作加上「持久」一词，因为多数优势很快被复制，就不再是优势。

senses.title: An advantage rooted in resources
senses.definition: an edge that comes from resources a firm owns that are rare and hard to imitate
senses.definitionCN: 来自企业拥有的稀缺且难以模仿的资源
senses.example: Rare earth deposits are a resource-based competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 稀土矿藏是一种基于资源的竞争优势。
senses.why: the resource-based view asks what the firm owns, not what it does, so the phrase shifts to stocks rather than actions.
senses.whyCN: 资源基础观问企业拥有什么而非做什么，因此这个短语转向「存量」而非「动作」。

senses.title: A locational advantage
senses.definition: an edge from being close to markets, suppliers, ports or skilled labour
senses.definitionCN: 因靠近市场、供应商、港口或熟练劳动力而获得的优势
senses.example: Proximity to the port is a locational competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 靠近港口是一种区位竞争优势。
senses.why: advantage can attach to a place, because distance still costs money even in a digital economy.
senses.whyCN: 优势可以附着在地点上，因为即使在数字经济中，距离仍然要花钱。

senses.title: First-mover advantage
senses.definition: an edge gained by entering a market before rivals and locking in customers or standards
senses.definitionCN: 先于对手进入市场并锁定顾客或标准而取得的优势
senses.example: Being first to the market gave the startup a competitive advantage.
senses.exampleCN: 率先进入市场给了这家初创企业竞争优势。
senses.why: the phrase covers timing as well as resources, since an early position can itself be the asset.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语也涵盖时机，因为靠前的位置本身就可以是资产。

senses.title: An edge for any organization
senses.titleCN: 任何组织相对对手的有利条件
senses.definition: the same idea applied to a team, university or charity rather than a business
senses.definitionCN: 同一观念被用于队伍、大学或慈善机构而非企业
senses.example: A well-drilled team can turn a competitive advantage into a win.
senses.exampleCN: 训练有素的队伍能把竞争优势转化为胜利。
senses.why: once rivals are anywhere, advantage follows them beyond commercial markets.
senses.whyCN: 一旦对手无处不在，优势就跟着越出商业市场。

intro.en: Competitive comes from Latin competere 'to strive together'. Advantage comes through Old French avantage from avant 'before', ultimately from Latin ab ante 'from before'. The phrase is twentieth-century strategy vocabulary. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: competitive 来自拉丁 competere「一起力争」。advantage 经古法语 avantage 上溯 avant「在前」，最终来自拉丁 ab ante「从前面」。整个短语是 20 世纪战略词汇。年代均为约数。

items.en: The phrase ab ante meant 'from before, in front of'. Its shortened form ante 'before' is the seed of the whole advantage family.
items.cn: ab ante 意为「从前面、在……之前」，其简式 ante「在前」是整族 advantage 词的种子。

items.en: Avant 'before' plus the noun suffix -age produced avantage, a position ahead of others or a profit gained from it.
items.cn: avant「在前」加名词后缀 -age 构成 avantage，指领先于他人的位置或由此得到的利益。

items.en: English borrowed advantage in the fourteenth century, first as a favourable position, then as a benefit or profit.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入 advantage，先指有利位置，后指好处或利益。

items.en: Competere joins com- 'together' to petere 'seek'; competitive entered English as an adjective for anything able to contend.
items.cn: competere 把 com-「共同」接在 petere「寻求」上；competitive 作为形容词进入英语，形容能够相争的事物。

items.en: Competitive advantage became central to business strategy writing in the 1980s, when analysts asked why some firms consistently outperform others.
items.cn: 20 世纪 80 年代，当分析者追问为何某些企业持续胜过其他企业时，competitive advantage 成为企业战略写作的核心。

items.en: The exact first printed use of the full phrase is not recorded; earlier economics used advantage and competitive separately. The Latin and French steps are documented.
items.cn: 完整短语的最早印刷用例没有确切记录；更早的经济学写作分开使用 advantage 与 competitive。拉丁与法语环节有据可查。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike words from the advantage family, including one that is a doublet rather than a derivative; group two holds near terms for an edge that are not identical to it.
note.cn: 第一组是 advantage 词族中易混的词，其中一个是对偶词而非派生词；第二组是表示「优势」的近义说法，与它并不完全等同。

entries.definition: From the same avant 'before' line, but it means to move forward in space or time, not to hold a favourable position.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 avant「在前」这条线，但意为在空间或时间上向前移动，而非占据有利位置。

entries.definition: Dis- added to advantage in English, naming an unfavourable position; it is not a Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: dis- 在英语中加在 advantage 上，指不利位置；它不是拉丁词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning favourable; a competitive advantage is the noun, while advantageous describes the condition.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「有利的」形容词；competitive advantage 是名词，而 advantageous 描述该条件。

entries.definition: The rival itself; an advantage exists only in relation to a competitor, but the two words name different things.
entries.definitionCN: 指对手本身；优势只在与竞争者相对时存在，但这两个词指称不同事物。

entries.definition: A small lead or sharpness over rivals; it is the everyday word for what competitive advantage states formally.
entries.definitionCN: 对对手的微小领先或锋利之处；它是竞争优势正式说法的日常版本。

entries.definition: A capability a firm possesses; a strength becomes an advantage only when buyers or rivals make it valuable.
entries.definitionCN: 企业拥有的能力；只有当买主或对手使其有价值时，能力才成为优势。

entries.definition: A resource with value; assets can support an advantage, but an asset by itself may be neither rare nor useful.
entries.definitionCN: 有价值的资源；资产可以支撑优势，但一项资产本身未必稀缺或有用。

entries.definition: The state of being better than another; it is a verdict, while competitive advantage is a market condition.
entries.definitionCN: 优于他者的状态；它是一种评判，而竞争优势是一种市场条件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: avant 'before' + -age: advantage is literally a position in front.
normal.cn: avant「在前」+ -age：advantage 字面上就是「靠前的位置」。

normal.en: The family runs advantage, advantageous, disadvantage, disadvantaged, competitive, competitor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 advantage、advantageous、disadvantage、disadvantaged、competitive、competitor。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the strategy sense: sustainable competitive advantage, source of competitive advantage.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出战略义：可持续竞争优势、竞争优势的来源。

normal.en: Strategy writing pairs it with three sources: cost, differentiation and focus.
normal.cn: 战略写作把它与三种来源配对：成本、差异化与聚焦。

normal.en: The everyday twin is competitive edge, used in speech more than in reports.
normal.cn: 日常的对应说法是 competitive edge，多用于口语而非报告。

abstract.en: Picture a runner with better shoes on the same starting line.
abstract.cn: 想象一名跑者站在同一条起跑线上，脚上却是一双更好的鞋。

abstract.en: Picture two stalls side by side, one with a shorter queue.
abstract.cn: 想象并排的两个摊位，其中一个队伍更短。

abstract.en: Picture a map where one warehouse sits closer to every road.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，其中一座仓库离每条路都更近。

examples.en: The firm's competitive advantage disappeared once the patent expired.
examples.cn: 专利一到期，这家企业的竞争优势就消失了。

examples.en: Training staff well can create a competitive advantage that rivals cannot buy.
examples.cn: 把员工培训好，可以创造对手买不到的竞争优势。

examples.en: Analysts asked which competitive advantage would survive the next price war.
examples.cn: 分析者追问哪一项竞争优势能挺过下一场价格战。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「competitive（竞争的）+ advantage（靠前的位置）」——在竞争中站得更靠前 → 竞争优势

root: competitive 来自拉丁 competere「一起力争」（com- + petere「寻求」）；advantage 经古法语 avantage 上溯 avant「在前」，最终来自拉丁 ab ante「从前面」。整个短语为 20 世纪战略用语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one lead: a firm stands ahead of its rivals, and that lead is then located in cost, in difference, in durability, in owned resources, in a place, in timing, and finally in any organization that has rivals.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「靠前」展开：企业站在对手前面，这个靠前再依次落在成本、差异、持久性、自有资源、地点、时机，最后落在任何有对手的组织上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner on the same starting line with better shoes.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条起跑线上，一名跑者穿着更好的鞋。

branches.en: THE PLAIN LEAD: any condition that puts a firm ahead.
branches.cn: 朴素的领先：任何使企业靠前的条件。

branches.en: TWO ROUTES: charge less, or offer what rivals do not.
branches.cn: 两条路径：收得更少，或提供对手没有的东西。

branches.en: DURABILITY AND OWNERSHIP: an edge that survives imitation, and one rooted in what the firm owns.
branches.cn: 持久与所有：经得住模仿的优势，以及扎根于企业自有资源的优势。

branches.en: PLACE AND TIMING: proximity to roads and ports, and the advantage of arriving first.
branches.cn: 地点与时机：靠近道路与港口，以及先到一步的好处。

branches.en: BEYOND BUSINESS: the same lead sought by a team, a school or a charity.
branches.cn: 越出商业：队伍、学校或慈善机构追求的同一个领先。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Latin-derived adjective of striving with a French-derived noun of being in front; neither half is a bare root.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源的「相争」形容词与法语来源的「在前」名词组合起来；两半都不是光秃的词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin petere and com- supply competitive and competitor; Latin ante, through French avant, supplies advantage, advantageous and disadvantage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 petere 与 com- 提供 competitive 与 competitor；拉丁 ante 经法语 avant 提供 advantage、advantageous 与 disadvantage。

items.structure: Latin preposition ante (before, in front of)
items.example: The Latin word survives inside advantage and advance.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词留在 advantage 与 advance 之中。

items.example: Height is an advantage in basketball.
items.exampleCN: 身高在篮球中是优势。

items.example: The early train is advantageous for commuters.
items.exampleCN: 早班车对通勤者有利。

items.example: Distance is a disadvantage for the shop.
items.exampleCN: 距离远是这家店的不利条件。

items.example: The programme serves disadvantaged students.
items.exampleCN: 该项目服务处境不利的学生。

items.example: Four firms compete for the tender.
items.exampleCN: 四家企业争夺这项招标。

items.example: The service is priced competitively.
items.exampleCN: 这项服务定价有竞争力。

items.example: A rival copied the design within a year.
items.exampleCN: 一家对手在一年内复制了设计。

items.example: The extra staff gave them an edge.
items.exampleCN: 多出的员工给了他们一点优势。

items.example: The land was bought advantageously before prices rose.
items.exampleCN: 这块地在涨价前被有利地买下。

definition_zh: 垄断；垄断企业；专卖权；独占
definition_en: exclusive control of a market or commodity by a single seller
core_image: 一条街只有一家店开门，橱窗上贴着唯一的价目表，顾客排成长队也别无选择
scene: 小镇上唯一的一家加油站挂出新的价目牌，排队的车主只能接受。A local monopoly can raise prices until customers travel to a distant substitute.
sceneCN: 这里 monopoly 指「由单一卖方控制的市场结构」（第 1 个义项：市场上只有一个卖方）；句意为地方性垄断可以把价格提高，直到顾客愿意去远处寻找替代品。图中可辨识物件：唯一的加油站、单一价目牌、排队车辆、远处的替代站点。

pos.zh: 垄断；垄断企业；专卖权；独占

senses.title: A market with one seller
senses.definition: a market structure in which a single seller supplies the whole demand and faces no direct rival
senses.definitionCN: 由单一卖方供应全部需求、没有直接对手的市场结构
senses.example: The island's ferry service is a monopoly with no alternative route.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上的渡轮服务是一种没有替代航线的垄断。
senses.why: monos 'single' plus polein 'sell' gives the literal reading: one seller for the whole market.
senses.whyCN: monos「单一」加 polein「卖」给出字面读法：整个市场只有一个卖方。

senses.title: An exclusive right granted by law
senses.definition: a legal privilege allowing one party alone to trade in a good or service
senses.definitionCN: 允许某一方独自经营某种商品或服务的法定特权
senses.example: The old charter gave the company a monopoly on salt.
senses.exampleCN: 旧特许状给了这家公司食盐的专营权。
senses.why: the Greek word first named a concession granted by a city, so the legal sense is older than the economic one.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词最初指城邦授予的特许，因此法律义比经济义更早。

senses.title: The commodity under exclusive control
senses.definition: the good or service that only one supplier is allowed or able to provide
senses.definitionCN: 只允许或只能够由一家供应商提供的商品或服务
senses.example: Broadcasting was once a monopoly of the state.
senses.exampleCN: 广播曾经是国家独占的事业。
senses.why: English allows the word to stand for the thing controlled, not only for the control itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许这个词指被控制的对象，而不只是控制本身。

senses.title: The firm that holds the market
senses.definition: the company or organization that enjoys exclusive control
senses.definitionCN: 享有独占控制权的公司或机构
senses.example: Regulators treated the railway as a monopoly and capped its fares.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者把这家铁路公司当作垄断企业，并限制其票价。
senses.why: metonymy turns the structure into the actor, so monopoly can mean the monopolist.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把结构变成行为者，于是 monopoly 可以指垄断企业。

senses.title: A state monopoly
senses.definition: exclusive government control of a trade, often for revenue or public order
senses.definitionCN: 政府对某项贸易的独占控制，常用于增加财政收入或维护公共秩序
senses.example: The tobacco monopoly supplies a large share of the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 烟草专卖提供了预算的很大一部分。
senses.why: early modern states used exclusive grants as a tax-collecting device, and the phrase kept that association.
senses.whyCN: 近代早期国家把专营特许当作征税工具，这个说法保留了这层联系。

senses.title: A temporary monopoly from a patent
senses.titleCN: 专利或版权带来的暂时独占
senses.definition: exclusive commercial use of an invention or work for a limited term
senses.definitionCN: 在有限期限内对某项发明或作品的独占商业使用
senses.example: The patent gave the maker a monopoly for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 专利给了制造商二十年的独占期。
senses.why: intellectual property is a deliberate, time-limited monopoly meant to reward disclosure.
senses.whyCN: 知识产权是一种有意设置、期限有限的垄断，用以奖励公开。

senses.title: A natural monopoly
senses.definition: a market where high fixed costs make one supplier cheaper than several
senses.definitionCN: 固定成本很高、使一家供应比多家供应更便宜的市场
senses.example: Water pipes form a natural monopoly because duplicating them is wasteful.
senses.exampleCN: 水管构成自然垄断，因为重复铺设是浪费。
senses.why: economists call it natural because the single supplier arises from cost structure, not from a legal grant.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家称之为「自然」，因为单一供应来自成本结构，而非法律授予。

senses.title: Exclusive possession of anything
senses.titleCN: 对任何事物的排他性掌控（比喻义）
senses.definition: complete control of a thing or topic so that others have no share
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物或话题的完全控制，使他人无从分享
senses.example: The city does not have a monopoly on good ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 好主意并非这座城市所独占。
senses.why: detached from trade, the word keeps only its core of being the sole holder.
senses.whyCN: 脱离贸易语境后，这个词只保留「唯一持有者」这一核心。

intro.en: Monopoly comes from Greek monopōlion 'exclusive right to sell', built on monos 'alone' and pōlein 'to sell', and enters English through Latin monopolium. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monopoly 来自希腊 monopōlion「独家售卖权」，由 monos「单独」与 pōlein「卖」构成，经拉丁 monopolium 进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Monos meant 'alone, single'. The same element opens monologue, monorail and monarchy, where it combines with different second terms.
items.cn: monos 意为「单独的、唯一的」。同一成分出现在 monologue、monorail 与 monarchy 的开头，与不同的第二成分组合。

items.en: Pōlein meant 'to sell'. The -poly of monopoly is this verb, not Greek polys 'many', and it has nothing to do with polis 'city'.
items.cn: pōlein 意为「卖」。monopoly 中的 -poly 是这个动词，而非希腊语 polys「多」，也与 polis「城邦」无关。

items.en: Monopōlion named an exclusive sale or a concession granted by a city, especially the right to sell a particular commodity.
items.cn: monopōlion 指独家售卖或城邦授予的特许，尤其是经营某种商品的专权。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as monopolium and used it for exclusive trading rights, including grants made by rulers.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊名词吸收为 monopolium，用于独家贸易权，包括统治者授予的特许。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the sixteenth century, first for royal grants and later for any single-seller market as economics developed.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入这个词，先指王室特许，随着经济学发展又指任何单一卖方市场。

items.en: The exact first English citation is approximate. The deeper origin of pōlein is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 最早的英语书证年代只是约数。pōlein 的更深来源属重构形式，并非有直接书证。

note.en: Group one holds neighbouring market structures whose Greek second elements are often confused; group two holds words for control or exclusive dealing that are not market structures.
note.cn: 第一组是第二成分常被混淆的邻近市场结构；第二组是表示控制或独家交易、但并非市场结构的词。

entries.definition: A market with a single buyer; its Greek second element is opsōnein 'to buy', so it is the mirror image of monopoly.
entries.definitionCN: 只有一个买方的市场；其希腊第二成分是 opsōnein「买」，因此是 monopoly 的镜像。

entries.definition: A market dominated by a small number of sellers; the second element is the same verb 'to sell', but the first is oligos 'few'.
entries.definitionCN: 由少数卖方支配的市场；第二成分同为「卖」这个动词，但第一成分是 oligos「少数」。

entries.definition: A market with two dominant sellers, built with Latin duo- on the same Greek selling element.
entries.definitionCN: 由两家主要卖方构成的市场，以拉丁 duo- 接同一个希腊「卖」成分。

entries.definition: The person or firm that holds a monopoly; the structure is monopoly, while the holder is the monopolist.
entries.definitionCN: 持有垄断地位的人或企业；结构是 monopoly，持有者则是 monopolist。

entries.definition: To gain control of a commodity by buying enough of it to dictate price; it is an action, not a market structure.
entries.definitionCN: 通过买下足够多的商品来控制价格；它是一种行为，而非市场结构。

entries.definition: The state of being restricted to one party; a monopoly is one legal or economic form of exclusivity.
entries.definitionCN: 仅限一方享有的状态；垄断是排他性的一种法律或经济形式。

entries.definition: An agreement among independent sellers to fix prices or divide markets; it imitates monopoly without a single seller.
entries.definitionCN: 独立卖方之间固定价格或划分市场的协议；它模仿垄断，却没有单一卖方。

entries.definition: In late nineteenth-century law, a trust was a combination of firms placed under shared trustees, the target of early antitrust law.
entries.definitionCN: 在 19 世纪后期的法律中，trust 指置于共同受托人下的企业联合，是早期反垄断法的对象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: monos 'single' + polein 'sell': one seller for the whole market.
normal.cn: monos「单一」+ polein「卖」：整个市场只有一个卖方。

normal.en: The family runs monopoly, monopolist, monopolize, monopolistic, monopolization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 monopoly、monopolist、monopolize、monopolistic、monopolization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the market sense: natural monopoly, state monopoly, monopoly power.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出市场义：自然垄断、国家专卖、垄断力量。

normal.en: The -poly here is 'sell', not 'many': oligopoly and duopoly use the same verb.
normal.cn: 这里的 -poly 是「卖」而非「多」：oligopoly 与 duopoly 用的是同一个动词。

normal.en: Its mirror image is monopsony, where one buyer faces many sellers.
normal.cn: 它的镜像是 monopsony，即一个买方面对许多卖方。

abstract.en: Picture a street with one lit window and a queue outside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街上只有一扇亮着的橱窗，门外排着队。

abstract.en: Picture a single key that opens every door in a building.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙能打开一栋楼里的每一扇门。

abstract.en: Picture one price tag that nobody on the street can undercut.
abstract.cn: 想象一张街上无人能压低的价签。

examples.en: The government broke up the monopoly after a decade of complaints.
examples.cn: 在十年投诉之后，政府拆分了这家垄断企业。

examples.en: A patent is a legal monopoly limited in time and scope.
examples.cn: 专利是一种在时间与范围上受限的法定垄断。

examples.en: No single company should have a monopoly on the public record.
examples.cn: 不应由任何一家公司独占公共记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mono（单一）+ poly（卖）」——整个市场只有一家在卖 → 垄断

root: 希腊 monos「单独」+ pōlein「卖」→ 希腊 monopōlion「独家售卖权」→ 拉丁 monopolium → 英语 monopoly。此处的 -poly 是「卖」，与 polys「多」及 polis「城邦」无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one seller: a single hand holds the whole supply, and that hold is then seen as a market structure, a legal grant, the commodity, the firm, a state trade, a patent term, a cost-driven case, and finally any exclusive possession.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个卖方展开：一只手握住全部供给，这个握有再依次被视为市场结构、法律授予、被控商品、企业本身、国家贸易、专利期限、成本造成的特例，最后是任何排他性占有。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lit shop window on a street, with a queue that has nowhere else to go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条街上只有一扇亮着的橱窗，队伍无处可去。

branches.en: STRUCTURE AND ACTOR: the single-seller market, and the firm that occupies it.
branches.cn: 结构与行为者：单一卖方市场，以及占据它的企业。

branches.en: GRANT AND OBJECT: a legal privilege, and the commodity that privilege covers.
branches.cn: 授予与对象：一项法律特权，以及该特权覆盖的商品。

branches.en: THE STATE: the same exclusive hold exercised for revenue or order.
branches.cn: 国家：为财政收入或秩序行使的同一种独占。

branches.en: TIME-LIMITED AND COST-DRIVEN: a patent term, and a market where fixed costs favour one supplier.
branches.cn: 限期与成本驱动：专利期限，以及固定成本偏向单一卖方的市场。

branches.en: ANY EXCLUSIVE HOLD: the word detached from trade and used for ideas or records.
branches.cn: 任何独占：脱离贸易后被用于思想或记录的词。

intro.en: Monopoly is a Greek compound filtered through Latin, so its two Greek elements can be read apart, and English then built a whole family on the noun.
intro.cn: monopoly 是经拉丁语过滤的希腊复合词，因此两个希腊成分可以分开读，英语随后又在这个名词上建起整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin monopolium carries the Greek compound into English; the family then adds -ist, -ize and -ation, while monopsony replaces the selling element with a buying one.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 monopolium 把这个希腊复合词带入英语；词族随后加 -ist、-ize 与 -ation，而 monopsony 把「卖」的成分换成「买」。

items.example: The element also opens monologue and monorail.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分也出现在 monologue 与 monorail 的开头。

items.example: The selling element is shared by oligopoly and duopoly.
items.exampleCN: 这个「卖」的成分由 oligopoly 与 duopoly 共享。

items.example: A local monopoly raised prices without fear.
items.exampleCN: 一家地方垄断者无所顾忌地提价。

items.example: The monopolist owned every pipeline in the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这家垄断企业拥有谷地里的每一条管道。

items.example: The monopolistic pricing drew regulatory attention.
items.exampleCN: 垄断定价引起了监管注意。

items.example: One firm monopolized the supply of spare parts.
items.exampleCN: 一家企业独占了备件供应。

items.example: Monopolization of the route took only three years.
items.exampleCN: 这条航线的垄断化只用了三年。

items.example: A monopsony can push purchase prices down.
items.exampleCN: 买方垄断可以把收购价压低。

items.example: The route is a duopoly of two airlines.
items.exampleCN: 这条航线是两家航空公司的双寡头。

items.example: An oligopoly kept prices stable for years.
items.exampleCN: 寡头格局让价格多年保持稳定。

latinEntries.meaning: a market with a single buyer

definition_zh: 垄断性的；垄断的；具有垄断特征的
definition_en: relating to or resembling a monopoly; tending to exclude competition
core_image: 一张市场地图上，原本散布的许多小店被涂成同一种颜色，只剩一面招牌
scene: 监管人员把一张市场分布图铺在桌上，图上几乎所有街区都被涂成同一家公司的颜色。Regulators accused the platform of monopolistic behaviour in the delivery market.
sceneCN: 这里 monopolistic 指「具有垄断特征的」（第 1 个义项：表现出单一卖方支配市场特征的）；句意为监管机构指控该平台在外卖市场有垄断行为。图中可辨识物件：市场分布图、单一颜色的街区、唯一的招牌、监管人员的手。

pos.zh: 垄断的；垄断性的；倾向排除竞争的

senses.title: Resembling a monopoly
senses.definition: showing the qualities of a market or practice controlled by a single seller
senses.definitionCN: 表现出由单一卖方控制的市场或做法所具有的特征
senses.example: The inquiry found monopolistic conditions in the ticket market.
senses.exampleCN: 调查发现票务市场存在垄断性状况。
senses.why: the suffix -istic means resembling or relating to, so the adjective describes a likeness to monopoly rather than its legal existence.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -istic 意为「像……的、与……相关的」，因此这个形容词描述与垄断相似，而非法律上的既成事实。

senses.title: Single-seller in structure
senses.definition: describing a market whose supply comes from one dominant provider
senses.definitionCN: 描述供给来自一个支配性提供者的市场
senses.example: The port is a monopolistic market with one operator.
senses.exampleCN: 这个港口是由一家运营商把持的垄断性市场。
senses.why: economists use the adjective for structures that approach a single seller even without a formal grant.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家用这个形容词描述即使没有正式授予、也接近单一卖方的结构。

senses.title: Conduct that tends to exclude rivals
senses.definition: business conduct that makes it hard for rivals to enter or survive
senses.definitionCN: 使对手难以进入或生存的商业做法
senses.example: Exclusive contracts were judged monopolistic.
senses.exampleCN: 排他合同被判定为垄断性做法。
senses.why: competition law shifts the adjective from structure to conduct, asking whether an act forecloses the market.
senses.whyCN: 竞争法把这个形容词从结构移到行为，追问某一行为是否封闭了市场。

senses.title: Pricing as if there were no rival
senses.definition: setting prices at the level a single seller could sustain without competition
senses.definitionCN: 按单一卖方在无竞争时所能维持的水平定价
senses.example: Monopolistic pricing pushed the price well above cost.
senses.exampleCN: 垄断定价把价格推到远高于成本的水平。
senses.why: the adjective names the price behaviour that the structure makes possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词指结构所使之成为可能的价格行为。

senses.title: Abuse of dominance in competition law
senses.titleCN: 反垄断法语境的滥用支配地位
senses.definition: conduct by a dominant firm that regulators treat as an abuse of its position
senses.definitionCN: 支配性企业作出、被监管者视为滥用其地位的行为
senses.example: The ruling classified the refusal to supply as monopolistic abuse.
senses.exampleCN: 裁决把拒绝供货归类为垄断性滥用。
senses.why: legal usage borrows the adjective because the statute must cover conduct that falls short of a full monopoly.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法借用这个形容词，因为法条须覆盖尚未构成完整垄断的行为。

senses.title: A firm large enough to set terms
senses.titleCN: 规模大到能设定条件的企业
senses.definition: describing a company whose size lets it dictate terms to suppliers or customers
senses.definitionCN: 描述规模使其能对供应商或顾客发号施令的公司
senses.example: A monopolistic buyer can dictate the price it pays farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 垄断性买方能单方面决定付给农民的价钱。
senses.why: the adjective can attach to a buyer as well, since size rather than selling is the key.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也可用于买方，因为关键在于规模而非卖方身份。

senses.title: State-run and exclusive
senses.definition: describing a trade reserved to a government body
senses.definitionCN: 描述由某一政府机构专属经营的行业
senses.example: The salt trade remained monopolistic until the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 盐业直到改革前都保持国家专营的格局。
senses.why: state monopolies supplied the earliest model, and the adjective still fits them.
senses.whyCN: 国家专卖提供了最早的范型，这个形容词至今仍适用于它们。

senses.title: Exclusive in a non-commercial sense
senses.definition: describing any arrangement in which one party shuts others out
senses.definitionCN: 描述任何由一方把他人排除在外的安排
senses.example: The club's monopolistic control of the archive worried historians.
senses.exampleCN: 该俱乐部对档案的排他性控制令历史学者担忧。
senses.why: once detached from markets, the adjective simply marks exclusion by one party.
senses.whyCN: 脱离市场后，这个形容词只标记由一方实施的排除。

intro.en: Monopolistic is an English derivative of monopoly, formed with the suffix complex -ist plus -ic, which reached English through French -istique from Latin -isticus and Greek -istikos. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monopolistic 是 monopoly 的英语派生词，由 -ist 加 -ic 的后缀组合构成；这一组合经法语 -istique 上溯拉丁 -isticus，再上溯希腊 -istikos。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek -istikos formed adjectives from agent nouns, often meaning 'skilled in' or 'concerned with'.
items.cn: 希腊 -istikos 从施事名词构成形容词，常表示「擅长于」或「与……有关」。

items.en: Latin -isticus carried the Greek suffix into learned vocabulary, where it described things belonging to a person or practice.
items.cn: 拉丁 -isticus 把这个希腊后缀带入学术词汇，描述属于某人或某种做法的事物。

items.en: French -istique passed the pattern to English adjectives such as artistic and characteristic.
items.cn: 法语 -istique 把这一模式传给英语形容词，如 artistic 与 characteristic。

items.en: English built monopolist with -ist and then monopolistic with -ic, so the adjective names what the holder does or resembles.
items.cn: 英语先用 -ist 构成 monopolist，再用 -ic 构成 monopolistic，因此这个形容词指持有者的作为或相似特征。

items.en: The adjective appears in nineteenth-century economic and legal writing, when states began regulating exclusive trading privileges.
items.cn: 这个形容词出现在 19 世纪的经济与法律写作中，当时各国开始规制独家贸易特权。

items.en: The exact first printed use is not recorded. Every step of the suffix chain is documented, so no part of the form is reconstructed.
items.cn: 最早印刷用例没有确切记录。后缀链条的每一步都有据可查，因此词形没有重构成分。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same family that name a different part of speech or a different market; group two holds near descriptors of market conduct.
note.cn: 第一组是同族中词性或所修饰市场不同的词；第二组是描述市场行为的近义形容词。

entries.definition: The participle of the verb, meaning that a market has already been taken over; it reports an act, not a standing trait.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的过去分词，表示市场已被占据；它报告一个动作，而非一种常态特征。

entries.definition: The person or firm holding the position; monopolistic describes the position or conduct, not the holder.
entries.definitionCN: 持有该地位的人或企业；monopolistic 描述地位或行为，而非持有者。

entries.definition: The buyer-side mirror, describing a market with one purchaser; the selling element has been replaced by a buying one.
entries.definitionCN: 买方一侧的镜像词，描述只有一个买主的市场；其中「卖」的成分已换成「买」。

entries.definition: Describing a market of few sellers; the form is parallel, but the first element changes from one to few.
entries.definitionCN: 描述少数卖方的市场；词形平行，但第一成分从「一」变为「少数」。

entries.definition: Describing conduct that harms competition; a regulator may call an act anti-competitive without calling the market monopolistic.
entries.definitionCN: 描述损害竞争的行为；监管者可以称某行为反竞争，而不称该市场垄断。

entries.definition: Holding the largest share or greatest influence; dominance is a precondition that competition law tests separately.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有最大份额或最强影响力；支配地位是竞争法另行检验的前提。

entries.definition: Limiting what others may do; a restrictive clause may or may not create a monopoly.
entries.definitionCN: 限制他人可为之事；限制性条款未必造成垄断。

entries.definition: Open to one party only; exclusivity can be lawful, while monopolistic conduct is the regulated case.
entries.definitionCN: 只对一方开放；排他可以是合法的，而垄断行为才是受规制的情形。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: monopoly + -ist + -ic: the adjective of the holder and the practice.
normal.cn: monopoly + -ist + -ic：由持有者与做法构成的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs monopoly, monopolist, monopolize, monopolization, monopolistic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 monopoly、monopolist、monopolize、monopolization、monopolistic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the legal sense: monopolistic behaviour, monopolistic pricing, monopolistic practices.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律义：垄断行为、垄断定价、垄断做法。
