normal.en: The suffix means 'resembling', so the word can describe conduct that is not yet a full monopoly.
normal.cn: 后缀意为「像……的」，因此这个词可以描述尚未构成完整垄断的行为。

normal.en: Its buyer-side twin is monopsonistic.
normal.cn: 它在买方一侧的对应词是 monopsonistic。

abstract.en: Picture a map where every block is painted the colour of one company.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，每个街区都被涂成同一家公司的颜色。

abstract.en: Picture a door with one keyhole and one key in the whole town.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，全城只有一把钥匙能开。

abstract.en: Picture a referee who also owns one of the teams.
abstract.cn: 想象一名裁判同时拥有一支参赛队伍。

examples.en: The court described the rebate scheme as monopolistic.
examples.cn: 法院把该返利方案描述为垄断性的。

examples.en: Monopolistic pricing can survive only behind high entry barriers.
examples.cn: 垄断定价只能在进入壁垒很高时维持。

examples.en: Not every dominant firm is monopolistic in the legal sense.
examples.cn: 并非每个支配性企业在法律意义上都是垄断的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「monopoly（垄断）+ istic（……的）」——带垄断味道的 → 垄断性的

root: monopoly（希腊 monos「单独」+ pōlein「卖」，经拉丁 monopolium）+ 后缀 -ist + -ic（经法语 -istique、拉丁 -isticus、希腊 -istikos），构成「具有垄断特征的」形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one likeness: something takes on the shape of a single-seller market, and that shape is then read as general resemblance, structure, conduct, pricing, legal abuse, buyer size, state trade, and finally any exclusion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种「相似」展开：某事物呈现出单一卖方市场的形状，这个形状再被读作总体相似、结构、行为、定价、法律滥用、买方规模、国家经营，最后是任何排除。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a market map painted in one colour, with a single sign left standing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张被涂成单一颜色的市场地图，只剩一面招牌立着。

branches.en: LIKENESS AND STRUCTURE: the general resemblance, then the near-single-seller market itself.
branches.cn: 相似与结构：总体相似，以及接近单一卖方的市场本身。

branches.en: CONDUCT AND PRICE: conduct that shuts rivals out, and the price such conduct permits.
branches.cn: 行为与价格：把对手关在门外的行为，以及这种行为所允许的价格。

branches.en: THE LEGAL LABEL: dominance abused rather than a market fully held.
branches.cn: 法律标签：被滥用的支配地位，而非被完整握有的市场。

branches.en: SIZE AND THE STATE: a buyer big enough to set terms, and a trade reserved to government.
branches.cn: 规模与国家：大到能设定条件的买方，以及保留给政府的行业。

branches.en: NON-COMMERCIAL EXCLUSION: one party shutting others out of an archive or a field.
branches.cn: 非商业排除：一方把他人挡在档案或领域之外。

intro.en: The adjective stacks a Greek noun, a Greek-derived agent suffix and an adjective suffix, so each layer can be read on its own.
intro.cn: 这个形容词叠了一个希腊名词、一个希腊来源的施事后缀和一个形容词后缀，因此每一层都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin monopolium is the base noun, and Latin -isticus (from Greek -istikos) supplies the ending seen in artistic and characteristic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 monopolium 是基础名词，拉丁 -isticus（来自希腊 -istikos）提供 artistic 与 characteristic 中可见的结尾。

items.example: One element of the compound means single.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词的一个成分意为「单一」。

items.example: The other element means to sell.
items.exampleCN: 另一个成分意为「卖」。

items.example: The monopoly ended with the new statute.
items.exampleCN: 新法终结了这项专营权。

items.example: The monopolist raised the access fee.
items.exampleCN: 垄断者提高了接入费。

items.example: Two firms monopolized the market.
items.exampleCN: 两家企业垄断了市场。

items.example: Monopolization took a decade.
items.exampleCN: 垄断化用了十年。

items.example: The practice was called monopolistic.
items.exampleCN: 这种做法被称为垄断性的。

items.example: The firm priced its service monopolistically.
items.exampleCN: 这家企业以垄断方式定价。

items.example: The airline market remains oligopolistic.
items.exampleCN: 航空市场仍呈寡头格局。

items.example: Buyers held monopsonistic power over growers.
items.exampleCN: 买方对种植者拥有买方垄断力量。

definition_zh: 垄断；独占；使…专营；独占（话题、注意力等）
definition_en: to control a market or resource exclusively, or to take up something so that others cannot share it
core_image: 一间会议室里，一个人从头说到尾，别人手里的发言纸始终没机会举起
scene: 会议桌旁，一个人不停接过话头，其他人举起的发言卡片又放回桌面。He monopolized the discussion so completely that no one else spoke.
sceneCN: 这里 monopolize 指「独占发言，使他人无法参与」（第 6 个义项：独占他人的注意力或时间）；句意为他把讨论完全占据，别人一句话也没说上。图中可辨识物件：会议长桌、发言卡片、放回桌面的纸卡、始终未亮的话筒。

pos.zh: 垄断；独占；使…专营；（在交谈中）独占

senses.title: Take over a market
senses.definition: to gain control of the supply of a good or service so that rivals cannot compete
senses.definitionCN: 取得某种商品或服务供给的控制权，使对手无法竞争
senses.example: The group monopolized the regional cement trade.
senses.exampleCN: 该集团垄断了区域水泥贸易。
senses.why: the verb turns the noun into an act: making a market into one seller's territory.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把名词变成动作：把一个市场变成单一卖方的地盘。

senses.title: Obtain an exclusive licence
senses.definition: to secure a legal right to be the only trader in a category
senses.definitionCN: 取得在法律上独家经营某一类别的权利
senses.example: The merchants monopolized the spice route under royal charter.
senses.exampleCN: 商人们凭王室特许垄断了香料航线。
senses.why: the earliest uses were legal, because exclusive trade began as a privilege granted by a ruler.
senses.whyCN: 最早的用法属法律义，因为独家贸易最初是由统治者授予的特权。

senses.title: Corner a resource or channel
senses.definition: to control enough of a resource or distribution channel to exclude others
senses.definitionCN: 控制足够的资源或分销渠道，从而把他人排除在外
senses.example: One buyer monopolized the supply of the rare ore.
senses.exampleCN: 一个买主独占了这种稀有矿石的供应。
senses.why: control of supply, not ownership of the whole industry, is enough to exclude rivals.
senses.whyCN: 控制供给、而非拥有整个行业，就足以排除对手。

senses.title: Hold information or bargaining power alone
senses.definition: to keep key information or access to a negotiation in one pair of hands
senses.definitionCN: 把关键信息或谈判接触渠道握在一方手中
senses.example: The broker monopolized the price data that both sides needed.
senses.exampleCN: 经纪人独占了双方都需要的价格数据。
senses.why: the word extends from goods to information because both can be withheld from rivals.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从商品延伸到信息，因为两者都可以对对手扣住不给。

senses.title: Bring a trade under state control
senses.definition: to place a trade under exclusive government ownership or licence
senses.definitionCN: 把某项贸易置于政府独家所有或特许之下
senses.example: The new government monopolized the sale of fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 新政府把燃料销售收归专营。
senses.why: states monopolize trades to collect revenue and to control supply, a use older than modern antitrust.
senses.whyCN: 国家把行业收归专营以征税并控制供给，这种用法早于现代反垄断。

senses.title: Take up all the talk or attention
senses.definition: to use so much of a conversation, room or moment that others get little or none
senses.definitionCN: 占用过多的谈话、空间或时刻，使他人所得甚少或全无
senses.example: He monopolized the discussion so completely that no one else spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 他把讨论完全占据，别人一句话也没说上。
senses.why: the figurative sense treats attention as a scarce good with only one supplier.
senses.whyCN: 比喻义把注意力当作只有一家供应的稀缺商品。

senses.title: Leave only one voice in a field
senses.titleCN: 使某领域只剩一种声音
senses.definition: to make one source so dominant that other views are effectively silenced
senses.definitionCN: 使某一来源过于强势，以致其他观点实际上被消音
senses.example: Two platforms monopolized the channels through which news reaches readers.
senses.exampleCN: 两个平台垄断了新闻到达读者的渠道。
senses.why: the market sense transfers to speech once distribution channels are owned by few hands.
senses.whyCN: 当分发渠道被少数人拥有，市场义就转移到言论领域。

senses.title: Keep something entirely to oneself
senses.definition: to keep a thing, feeling or role so completely that no one else shares it
senses.definitionCN: 把某物、某种感受或某个角色握得如此之紧，使他人无从分享
senses.example: She monopolized the role of peacemaker in the family.
senses.exampleCN: 她把家中和事佬的角色独占了下来。
senses.why: stripped of markets, the verb keeps only the core of holding alone.
senses.whyCN: 去掉市场语境后，这个动词只保留「独自握住」这一核心。

intro.en: Monopolize is English monopoly plus the verb suffix -ize, which came from Greek -izein through Latin -izare and French -iser. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monopolize 是英语 monopoly 加动词后缀 -ize 构成；-ize 经法语 -iser、拉丁 -izare 上溯希腊 -izein。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek -izein formed verbs meaning 'to do, make or act as', as in baptizein and organizein.
items.cn: 希腊 -izein 构成意为「做、使、充当」的动词，如 baptizein 与 organizein。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek suffix as -izare and used it for verbs of making or following a practice.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊后缀借为 -izare，用于表示「使成为」或「依照某种做法行事」的动词。

items.en: French -iser carried the pattern into verbs such as organiser, which English then borrowed with -ize.
items.cn: 法语 -iser 把这一模式带入 organiser 一类动词，英语随后以 -ize 借入。

items.en: Monopoly plus -ize produced a verb recorded in the seventeenth century, first for obtaining exclusive trading rights.
items.cn: monopoly 加 -ize 构成的动词在 17 世纪已有记录，最初指取得独家贸易权。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the verb was used figuratively for taking up a conversation or a person's time, because attention behaves like a scarce supply.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，这个动词已被比喻性地用于占据谈话或他人时间，因为注意力表现得像稀缺供给。

items.en: The exact first printed use is approximate. The verb was formed in English, so it has no single Latin source.
items.cn: 最早印刷用例年代只是约数。这个动词是在英语中构成的，因此没有单一的拉丁语来源。

note.en: Group one holds family members that are nouns or adjectives rather than verbs; group two holds verbs of taking over that differ in scope or tone.
note.cn: 第一组是同族中的名词或形容词，而非动词；第二组是表示「占据」的动词，范围或语气不同。

entries.definition: The market position itself; monopolize names the act of creating or holding it.
entries.definitionCN: 市场地位本身；monopolize 指创造或持有这一地位的行为。

entries.definition: The holder of the position; the verb can be done by a monopolist but is not the holder.
entries.definitionCN: 该地位的持有者；动词可由垄断者实施，但动词并不指持有者。

entries.definition: The act or process named as a noun, often in competition-law filings; it is the result, not the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 以名词形式指称的行为或过程，常用于竞争法文书；它是结果，而非正在进行的动作。

entries.definition: To remove a monopoly, built with the negative prefix de-; it is the opposite operation, not a variant.
entries.definitionCN: 以否定前缀 de- 构成，意为取消垄断；这是相反的操作，而非同一动词的变体。

entries.definition: To hold the largest share or influence; a firm can dominate without controlling the whole supply.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有最大份额或影响力；企业可以支配市场，却未控制全部供给。

entries.definition: To buy enough of a commodity to control its price; it is narrower and often temporary.
entries.definitionCN: 买下足够多的商品以控制价格；范围更窄，且常是暂时的。

entries.definition: To keep something for oneself in a greedy way; it fits conversation and space better than markets.
entries.definitionCN: 贪心地据为己有；比用于市场更贴合谈话与空间。

entries.definition: To occupy completely, as a task engrosses a worker; it stresses absorption rather than exclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 完全占用，如工作使人全神贯注；强调被吸收，而非被排除。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: monopoly + -ize: to make a market into one seller's holding.
normal.cn: monopoly + -ize：把一个市场变成一个卖方的持有物。

normal.en: The family runs monopoly, monopolist, monopolistic, monopolization, monopolize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 monopoly、monopolist、monopolistic、monopolization、monopolize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the market sense: monopolize the market, monopolize trade, monopolize resources.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出市场义：垄断市场、垄断贸易、独占资源。

normal.en: The talk sense is marked by its object: monopolize the conversation, monopolize attention.
normal.cn: 谈话义由宾语标出：独占谈话、独占注意力。

normal.en: The reverse verb is demonopolize, built with the negative prefix.
normal.cn: 相反的动词是 demonopolize，以否定前缀构成。

abstract.en: Picture one speaker holding the floor while cards stay flat on the table.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人占着发言权，卡片一直平放在桌上。

abstract.en: Picture one shop buying every crate before anyone else can bid.
abstract.cn: 想象一家店在别人出价前买走每一只木箱。

abstract.en: Picture a single lamp lighting a room so that no other lamp is switched on.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯照亮整个房间，其他灯都不必打开。

examples.en: The platform tried to monopolize the market for delivery software.
examples.cn: 该平台试图垄断配送软件市场。

examples.en: One guest monopolized the dinner conversation for an hour.
examples.cn: 一位客人把晚餐谈话独占了一小时。

examples.en: Regulators ordered the firm to demonopolize the supply of spare parts.
examples.cn: 监管者命令该企业打破备件供应的垄断。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「monopoly（垄断）+ ize（使……）」——使整个市场只剩自己 → 垄断、独占

root: 英语 monopoly（希腊 monos「单独」+ pōlein「卖」，经拉丁 monopolium）+ 动词后缀 -ize（经法语 -iser、拉丁 -izare、希腊 -izein）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of taking: a single hand takes the whole supply, and the taking is then applied to a licence, a channel, information, a state trade, a conversation, a field of speech, and finally to anything held entirely alone.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「拿取」动作展开：一只手拿走全部供给，这个拿取再依次用于许可、渠道、信息、国家行业、一场谈话、一个言论领域，最后是完全独自握有的任何事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one speaker holding the floor while everyone else's cards stay on the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人占着发言权，其他人的卡片都留在桌上。

branches.en: MARKET AND RIGHT: taking the market, and taking the legal privilege that protects the taking.
branches.cn: 市场与权利：拿走市场，以及拿走保护这一拿取的法律特权。

branches.en: CHANNEL AND INFORMATION: control of supply lines, then control of what negotiators know.
branches.cn: 渠道与信息：控制供给线，再控制谈判者所知。

branches.en: THE STATE: a trade taken into public ownership or licence.
branches.cn: 国家：把行业收进公有或专营许可。

branches.en: FLOOR AND FIELD: taking a conversation, then taking the channels through which a field speaks.
branches.cn: 发言权与领域：拿走一场谈话，再拿走一个领域发声的渠道。

branches.en: ANYTHING HELD ALONE: a role or feeling kept so tightly that no one shares it.
branches.cn: 独自握有：某个角色或感受被握得太紧，无人分享。

intro.en: The verb is a noun plus a borrowed verb suffix, so it reads as 'make monopoly' before any figurative use.
intro.cn: 这个动词由名词加借来的动词后缀构成，因此在任何比喻用法之前，它的读法是「使成垄断」。

latinIntro.en: Latin monopolium supplies the noun, and -izare (from Greek -izein) supplies the verb ending; English also built demonopolize with de-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 monopolium 提供名词，-izare（来自希腊 -izein）提供动词词尾；英语还用 de- 构成 demonopolize。

items.example: The first element means single.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分意为「单一」。

items.example: The second element means sell.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分意为「卖」。

items.example: The charter created a monopoly.
items.exampleCN: 特许状创设了一项专营权。

items.example: One firm monopolized the trade.
items.exampleCN: 一家企业垄断了这项贸易。

items.example: The market was monopolized within a year.
items.exampleCN: 市场在一年内被垄断。

items.meaning: in the act of taking over
items.example: A monopolizing buyer drove prices down.
items.exampleCN: 一个正在垄断的买方压低了价格。

items.meaning: the act or result of monopolizing
items.example: The case concerned the monopolization of a route.
items.exampleCN: 该案涉及一条航线的垄断化。

items.example: The monopolizer left no room for rivals.
items.exampleCN: 独占者没给对手留下空间。

items.example: The state moved to demonopolize the trade.
items.exampleCN: 国家着手取消这项贸易的垄断。

items.example: The board reviewed the monopolistic contract.
items.exampleCN: 董事会审查了这份垄断性合同。

latinEntries.meaning: one who holds an exclusive trade

definition_en: a market structure in which a few sellers dominate and each can affect price
core_image: 四家店门口挂着几乎相同的价目牌，价格一动，其余三家当天就跟着改
scene: 商业街上四家手机店贴着几乎一样的价目牌，一家改了数字，其余三家当天跟着改。An oligopoly often produces stable prices and heavy advertising rather than price wars.
sceneCN: 这里 oligopoly 指「少数卖方共同支配的市场结构」（第 1 个义项：由少数几家卖方主导的市场）；句意为寡头市场常带来稳定的价格与大量广告，而非价格战。图中可辨识物件：四家相邻店铺、几乎相同的价目牌、同日改价的痕迹、广告牌。

senses.title: A market run by a few sellers
senses.titleCN: 由少数卖方支配的市场
senses.definition: a market in which a small number of sellers supply most of the demand and each watches the others
senses.definitionCN: 由少数卖方供应大部分需求、且各自紧盯其余几家的市场
senses.example: The mobile network market is an oligopoly of three operators.
senses.exampleCN: 移动网络市场是三家运营商构成的寡头格局。
senses.why: oligos 'few' plus polein 'sell' says exactly what the structure is: selling by the few.
senses.whyCN: oligos「少数」加 polein「卖」正好说明这种结构：由少数人出售。

senses.title: The group of dominant firms
senses.titleCN: 支配市场的寡头企业群体
senses.definition: the small set of firms that together control supply
senses.definitionCN: 共同控制供给的那一小群企业
senses.example: The oligopoly met privately before the public tariff review.
senses.exampleCN: 这些寡头企业在公开费率审议前私下会面。
senses.why: metonymy lets the structure stand for the firms that occupy it.
senses.whyCN: 转喻使结构可以指占据它的那些企业。

senses.title: A tight oligopoly
senses.definition: a market where the leading few hold a very high combined share
senses.definitionCN: 少数领先者合计占有很高份额的市场
senses.example: A tight oligopoly makes collusion easier to sustain.
senses.exampleCN: 紧寡头使合谋更容易维持。
senses.why: economists grade oligopoly by concentration, so the phrase takes a qualifier when the few are very few.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家按集中度给寡头分级，因此当少数者极少时会加限定语。

senses.title: A loose oligopoly
senses.definition: a market with several significant sellers and a competitive fringe
senses.definitionCN: 有几家重要卖方、外围仍有竞争者的市场
senses.example: A loose oligopoly behaves almost like a competitive market at the edges.
senses.exampleCN: 松寡头在外围表现得几乎像竞争性市场。
senses.why: the same structure shades into competition when the leading share is lower.
senses.whyCN: 当领先份额较低时，同一结构会渐变为竞争。

senses.title: A differentiated oligopoly
senses.definition: an oligopoly whose sellers compete with recognizably different products
senses.definitionCN: 卖方以明显不同的产品竞争的市场
senses.example: Airlines form a differentiated oligopoly through routes and service.
senses.exampleCN: 航空公司通过航线与服务形成差异寡头。
senses.why: when products differ, rivalry runs through branding and features rather than price alone.
senses.whyCN: 当产品有差异，竞争就通过品牌与功能展开，而非只靠价格。

senses.title: A homogeneous oligopoly
senses.definition: an oligopoly whose sellers offer nearly identical products
senses.definitionCN: 卖方提供几乎相同产品的市场
senses.example: A homogeneous oligopoly tends to compete on price because nothing else differs.
senses.exampleCN: 同质寡头往往在价格上竞争，因为没有别的差异。
senses.why: with identical goods, the only visible lever left is price.
senses.whyCN: 当商品相同，唯一可见的杠杆就是价格。

senses.title: Oligopoly pricing and tacit collusion
senses.definition: the pattern in which a few sellers keep prices aligned without a formal agreement
senses.definitionCN: 少数卖方在没有正式协议的情况下保持价格一致的模式
senses.example: Oligopoly pricing can look competitive while margins stay high.
senses.exampleCN: 寡头定价看似竞争，利润率却居高不下。
senses.why: each seller knows that a price cut will be matched, so the few settle into a quiet equilibrium.
senses.whyCN: 每个卖方都知道降价会被跟随，于是少数几家进入一种安静的均衡。

senses.title: Any field held by a few
senses.titleCN: 任何由少数几方把持的领域（比喻义）
senses.definition: a domain in which a handful of actors control access or output
senses.definitionCN: 由少数行为者控制准入或产出的领域
senses.example: The newspaper market became an oligopoly of two families.
senses.exampleCN: 报业市场成了两个家族把持的寡头格局。
senses.why: the word leaves economics once any field is controlled by a small group.
senses.whyCN: 一旦任何领域被小群体控制，这个词就走出经济学。

intro.en: Oligopoly is a modern English compound of Greek oligos 'few' and pōlein 'to sell', modelled on monopoly. It was coined in economic writing in the late nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oligopoly 是由希腊 oligos「少数」与 pōlein「卖」构成的现代英语复合词，仿 monopoly 而造，于 19 世纪后期的经济学写作中出现。年代均为约数。

items.en: Oligos meant 'few, little'. The same element opens oligarchy, where it joins archein 'to rule' rather than a verb of selling.
items.cn: oligos 意为「少数、少量」。同一成分出现在 oligarchy 的开头，那里它与 archein「统治」结合，而非与「卖」结合。

items.en: Pōlein 'to sell' also supplies the -poly of monopoly and duopoly; it is not the polys meaning 'many'.
items.cn: pōlein「卖」也提供 monopoly 与 duopoly 中的 -poly；它不是表示「多」的 polys。

items.en: Writers replaced the monos 'one' of monopoly with oligos 'few', keeping the selling element unchanged.
items.cn: 写作者把 monopoly 中的 monos「一」换成 oligos「少数」，保留不变的「卖」成分。

items.en: The term is generally dated to late nineteenth-century economics; the exact coiner is disputed, and several writers are proposed.
items.cn: 这个词一般被定在 19 世纪后期的经济学中；确切造词者有争议，有数位写作者被提出。

items.en: Twentieth-century industrial economics gave the concept its standard tests: concentration ratios, price parallelism and entry barriers.
items.cn: 20 世纪的产业经济学为这一概念提供了标准检验：集中度比率、价格平行与进入壁垒。

items.en: The exact first citation is not recorded; the coiner is disputed. Every morpheme in the compound is documented Greek.
items.cn: 最早书证没有确切记录，造词者有争议。复合词中的每个语素都是有据的希腊语。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes built on oligos or on the selling element; group two holds related market terms that are not a structure of few sellers.
note.cn: 第一组是以 oligos 或「卖」这个成分为基础、容易混淆的词；第二组是相关市场术语，但并非「少数卖方」结构。

entries.definition: Government by a small group; it shares oligos but joins it to archein 'to rule', not to a verb of selling.
entries.definitionCN: 由小群体统治；它共享 oligos，却接 archein「统治」，而非「卖」这个动词。

entries.definition: A single-seller market; oligopoly is the few-seller version of the same selling element.
entries.definitionCN: 单一卖方市场；oligopoly 是同一「卖」成分的少数卖方版本。

entries.definition: A two-seller market, the smallest case of an oligopoly rather than a separate structure.
entries.definitionCN: 两家卖方市场，是寡头的最小情形，而非另一种结构。

entries.definition: The adjective describing such a market; oligopoly is the noun for the structure itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述此类市场的形容词；oligopoly 是结构本身的名词。

entries.definition: A formal or informal agreement among sellers to fix prices or share markets; an oligopoly may host a cartel but need not.
entries.definitionCN: 卖方之间固定价格或划分市场的正式或非正式协议；寡头市场可能容纳卡特尔，但不必有。

entries.definition: The share of a market held by the largest firms; it is a measure of oligopoly, not the structure itself.
entries.definitionCN: 最大几家企业在市场中的份额；它是寡头的度量，而非结构本身。

entries.definition: The capacity to raise price above competitive levels; a firm can hold it without a market being an oligopoly.
entries.definitionCN: 把价格提高到竞争水平之上的能力；企业可以拥有它，而市场未必是寡头。

entries.definition: A temporary group formed for one project; it is a collaboration, not a lasting market structure.
entries.definitionCN: 为一个项目临时组成的集团；它是合作，而非持久市场结构。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: oligos 'few' + polein 'sell': selling by a few.
normal.cn: oligos「少数」+ polein「卖」：由少数人出售。

normal.en: The family runs oligopoly, oligopolistic, oligopolist, duopoly, monopoly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 oligopoly、oligopolistic、oligopolist、duopoly、monopoly。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the market sense: tight oligopoly, loose oligopoly, oligopoly pricing.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出市场义：紧寡头、松寡头、寡头定价。

normal.en: The -poly is again 'sell', the same element as in monopoly and duopoly.
normal.cn: 这里的 -poly 仍是「卖」，与 monopoly、duopoly 中的成分相同。

normal.en: The few can behave like one seller without any formal agreement.
normal.cn: 这少数几家可以在没有正式协议时表现得像一个卖方。

abstract.en: Picture four shop signs that change on the same afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象四块店招在同一个下午一起更换。

abstract.en: Picture a table with four chairs and every other chair removed.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子原是四把椅子，其余都被搬走。

abstract.en: Picture four chess pieces circling one square, none willing to move first.
abstract.cn: 想象四枚棋子围着一个格子，谁都不肯先动。

examples.en: The airline route is an oligopoly shared by two carriers.
examples.cn: 这条航线是两家航空公司共享的寡头格局。

examples.en: Oligopoly pricing often survives because each seller expects retaliation.
examples.cn: 寡头定价常能维持，因为每个卖方都预期会遭报复。

examples.en: A tight oligopoly can keep new entrants out for years.
examples.cn: 紧寡头可以把新进入者挡在门外多年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oligo（少数）+ poly（卖）」——少数几家在卖 → 寡头垄断

root: 希腊 oligos「少数」+ pōlein「卖」→ 仿 monopoly 造的英语复合词 oligopoly，19 世纪后期进入经济学；-poly 与 polys「多」无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one small group: a few sellers hold the market, and that group is then seen as the structure, the firms, a tight or loose case, a differentiated or identical case, the pricing pattern, and finally any field held by a few.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个小群体展开：少数卖方握住市场，这个群体再被看作结构、企业、紧或松的情形、有差异或无差异的情形、定价模式，最后是任何由少数把持的领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four shop signs that all change on the same afternoon.
core.cn: 核心意象：四块店招在同一个下午一起更换。

branches.en: STRUCTURE AND FIRMS: the few-seller market, and the few firms that occupy it.
branches.cn: 结构与企业：少数卖方市场，以及占据它的少数企业。

branches.en: TIGHT AND LOOSE: concentration graded from very high to merely significant.
branches.cn: 紧与松：集中度从极高到仅属显著的分级。

branches.en: DIFFERENCE AND SAMENESS: whether the few sell unlike goods or near-identical ones.
branches.cn: 差异与相同：少数几家卖的是不同商品还是几乎相同的商品。

branches.en: ALIGNED PRICES: the quiet equilibrium that the few can reach without a contract.
branches.cn: 价格一致：少数几家无需合同即可达到的安静均衡。

branches.en: ANY SMALL GROUP: newspapers, platforms or any field held by a handful.
branches.cn: 任何小群体：报纸、平台或任何被少数把持的领域。

intro.en: The word is a Greek-style compound built inside English, so its two elements are free Greek roots rather than a root with suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词是在英语内部构成的希腊式复合词，因此两个成分是自由的希腊词根，而非词根加后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor for the compound itself; Latin monopolium supplied the model, and Greek oligos and pōlein supplied the parts.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词本身没有拉丁语祖先；拉丁 monopolium 提供了模型，希腊 oligos 与 pōlein 提供了构件。

items.example: The element also opens oligarchy.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分也出现在 oligarchy 的开头。

items.example: The selling element is shared with monopoly.
items.exampleCN: 这个「卖」的成分与 monopoly 共享。

items.example: The route became an oligopoly.
items.exampleCN: 这条航线成了寡头格局。

items.example: Each oligopolist watched the others.
items.exampleCN: 每个寡头都盯着其余几家。

items.example: The sector has an oligopolistic shape.
items.exampleCN: 该行业呈寡头形态。

items.meaning: in the manner of few sellers
items.example: The firms priced oligopolistically.
items.exampleCN: 这些企业以寡头方式定价。

items.example: The airport is a duopoly of two handlers.
items.exampleCN: 该机场是两家地服公司的双寡头。

items.example: The railway was a legal monopoly.
items.exampleCN: 这条铁路曾是法定垄断。

items.example: A monopsony faces many growers.
items.exampleCN: 买方垄断面对许多种植者。

items.example: The club was run by a small oligarchy.
items.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部由一个小寡头集团管理。

definition_zh: 寡头垄断的；寡头市场的
definition_en: relating to a market dominated by a few sellers
core_image: 棋盘上只留下四枚同色棋子，其余格子空着，四枚棋子互相牵制
scene: 棋盘上只剩四枚同色棋子，彼此隔着几格，谁也不肯先动。The airline industry remains oligopolistic despite repeated attempts at liberalization.
sceneCN: 这里 oligopolistic 指「由少数卖方主导的」（第 1 个义项：具有寡头市场结构特征的）；句意为尽管多次推动自由化，航空业仍呈寡头格局。图中可辨识物件：四枚同色棋子、空棋盘格、相互牵制的距离、未动的棋子。

pos.zh: 寡头垄断的；寡头市场的

senses.title: Having the shape of few-seller market
senses.titleCN: 呈少数卖方市场形态的
senses.definition: describing a market whose supply is concentrated in a small number of firms
senses.definitionCN: 描述供给集中在少数几家企业的市场
senses.example: The telecom sector has an oligopolistic shape.
senses.exampleCN: 电信行业呈寡头形态。
senses.why: oligopoly plus -istic gives the adjective of resemblance, parallel to monopolistic.
senses.whyCN: oligopoly 加 -istic 构成表示相似的形容词，与 monopolistic 平行。

senses.title: Pricing by a few sellers
senses.definition: describing prices set by a small group that watches one another
senses.definitionCN: 描述由相互观望的小群体设定的价格
senses.example: Oligopolistic pricing kept fares almost equal across the three airlines.
senses.exampleCN: 寡头定价使三家航空公司的票价几乎相同。
senses.why: the adjective attaches to the price behaviour that the structure produces.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词附着于该结构所产生的价格行为。

senses.title: Rivalry among the few
senses.definition: describing competition in which each move is answered by the others
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种每一步都被其余几家回应的竞争
senses.example: Oligopolistic competition runs through advertising rather than price.
senses.exampleCN: 寡头竞争通过广告而非价格展开。
senses.why: with few players, every action is visible, so rivalry becomes a sequence of responses.
senses.whyCN: 参与者少，每个动作都可见，竞争便成为一连串回应。

senses.title: Given to tacit collusion
senses.definition: describing a market where the few can align without a formal agreement
senses.definitionCN: 描述少数几家无需正式协议就能取得一致的市场
senses.example: The regulator found oligopolistic coordination in fuel surcharges.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者发现燃油附加费存在寡头式协同。
senses.why: the adjective can describe behaviour as well as structure, and collusion is the behaviour most feared.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词既可描述结构也可描述行为，而合谋是最受担忧的行为。

senses.title: Belonging to a highly concentrated industry
senses.definition: describing an industry where the top few hold most of the market
senses.definitionCN: 描述前几家占有大部分市场的产业
senses.example: The rating agencies form an oligopolistic industry of three firms.
senses.exampleCN: 评级机构构成由三家企业组成的寡头产业。
senses.why: concentration ratios give the adjective a measurable threshold in industrial economics.
senses.whyCN: 集中度比率在产业经济学中给这个形容词一个可测量的门槛。

senses.title: Behind high entry barriers
senses.titleCN: 处于高进入壁垒之后的
senses.definition: describing a market where the few are protected by costs or rules that block newcomers
senses.definitionCN: 描述少数几家受成本或规则保护、新来者难以进入的市场
senses.example: An oligopolistic market can persist because new refineries are too expensive.
senses.exampleCN: 寡头市场能够持续，因为新建炼厂过于昂贵。
senses.why: the few survive only while entry stays hard, so the adjective often implies a barrier.
senses.whyCN: 只有当进入仍然困难时少数几家才能存活，因此这个形容词常含壁垒之意。

senses.title: As regulators describe a sector
senses.titleCN: 监管者描述某一行业时的用语
senses.definition: the label competition authorities use for a sector they consider too concentrated
senses.definitionCN: 竞争主管机构用来指称其认为过于集中的行业的标签
senses.example: The report called the funeral market oligopolistic and recommended review.
senses.exampleCN: 报告称殡葬市场为寡头市场，并建议审查。
senses.why: legal usage prefers the adjective because it describes a condition without alleging a specific violation.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法偏好这个形容词，因为它描述一种状态，而不指控具体违法行为。

senses.title: Held by a few in any field
senses.titleCN: 任何领域由少数把持的
senses.definition: describing any domain where a handful of actors control access
senses.definitionCN: 描述任何由少数行为者控制准入的领域
senses.example: The awards circuit remains oligopolistic, with four studios taking most nominations.
senses.exampleCN: 评奖圈仍呈寡头格局，四家制片厂拿走大部分提名。
senses.why: the adjective leaves economics once access anywhere is controlled by a small group.
senses.whyCN: 一旦任何领域的准入被小群体控制，这个形容词就走出经济学。

intro.en: Oligopolistic is an English derivative of oligopoly, formed with the suffix complex -ist plus -ic, the same pattern as monopolistic. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oligopolistic 是 oligopoly 的英语派生词，由 -ist 加 -ic 的后缀组合构成，与 monopolistic 同一模式。年代均为约数。

items.en: Oligos 'few' supplies the first element, the same root that opens oligarchy.
items.cn: oligos「少数」提供第一成分，与 oligarchy 开头同一词根。

items.en: Pōlein 'to sell' supplies the second element, unchanged from monopoly and duopoly.
items.cn: pōlein「卖」提供第二成分，与 monopoly、duopoly 中相同。

items.en: The noun was coined in late nineteenth-century economics on the model of monopoly.
items.cn: 这个名词于 19 世纪后期仿 monopoly 在经济学中造出。

items.en: English added -ist for a participant and -ic for the relating adjective, so oligopolist came before oligopolistic.
items.cn: 英语先加 -ist 表示参与者，再加 -ic 构成关系形容词，因此 oligopolist 先于 oligopolistic。

items.en: The adjective appears in twentieth-century industrial economics, once concentration ratios made few-seller markets measurable.
items.cn: 这个形容词出现在 20 世纪产业经济学中，当时集中度比率使少数卖方市场变得可测量。

items.en: The exact first printed use is not recorded. The suffix chain is fully documented and the Greek elements are attested.
items.cn: 最早印刷用例没有确切记录。后缀链条有完整书证，希腊成分也有据可查。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same compound and one same-root look-alike; group two holds adjectives that describe concentration or exclusion without naming the structure.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该复合词的词形，以及一个同根形近词；第二组是描述集中或排除、却不指称该结构的形容词。

entries.definition: The structure itself; oligopolistic is the adjective that describes it.
entries.definitionCN: 结构本身；oligopolistic 是描述它的形容词。

entries.definition: The parallel adjective for a single dominant seller; the suffix is the same, the first element is not.
entries.definitionCN: 平行形容词，用于单一支配卖方；后缀相同，第一成分不同。

entries.definition: From oligos plus archein 'to rule', meaning governed by a small group; its second element is political, not commercial.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 oligos 加 archein「统治」，意为由小群体治理；第二成分是政治的，而非商业的。

entries.definition: The adjective for exactly two sellers, the narrowest case of an oligopolistic market.
entries.definitionCN: 恰好两家卖方的形容词，是寡头市场中最窄的情形。

entries.definition: Describing a market where a large share sits with few firms; concentration is a measure, not a structure.
entries.definitionCN: 描述很大份额集中于少数企业的市场；集中度是一种度量，而非结构。

entries.definition: Describing an industry organized through agreements; an oligopolistic market may be cartelized, but not all are.
entries.definitionCN: 描述通过协议组织起来的产业；寡头市场可能被卡特尔化，但并非全都如此。

entries.definition: Describing terms that do not reflect rivalry; it names the result, while oligopolistic names the structure.
entries.definitionCN: 描述不反映竞争的条款；它指结果，而 oligopolistic 指结构。

entries.definition: Describing practices that limit what others may do; restrictive conduct can occur in a market that is not oligopolistic.
entries.definitionCN: 描述限制他人可为之事的行为；限制性行为也可发生在非寡头市场。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: oligopoly + -ist + -ic: the adjective of the few-seller structure.
normal.cn: oligopoly + -ist + -ic：少数卖方结构的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs oligopoly, oligopolist, oligopolistically, duopoly, monopoly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 oligopoly、oligopolist、oligopolistically、duopoly、monopoly。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the market sense: oligopolistic market, oligopolistic pricing, oligopolistic competition.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出市场义：寡头市场、寡头定价、寡头竞争。

normal.en: Its parallel is monopolistic: same suffix, first element changed from one to few.
normal.cn: 它的平行词是 monopolistic：后缀相同，第一成分从「一」变为「少数」。

normal.en: The look-alike oligarchic uses the root for rule, not the root for selling.
normal.cn: 形近词 oligarchic 用的是「统治」词根，而非「卖」词根。

abstract.en: Picture four pieces on a board with every other square empty.
abstract.cn: 想象棋盘上只剩四枚棋子，其余格子全空。

abstract.en: Picture four doors on one corridor and no other corridor to enter.
abstract.cn: 想象一条走廊上只有四扇门，没有别的走廊可进。

abstract.en: Picture four prices written on one board in the same handwriting.
abstract.cn: 想象四家价格写在同一块牌上，笔迹都一样。

examples.en: The market for operating systems is oligopolistic rather than open.
examples.cn: 操作系统市场呈寡头格局，而非开放市场。

examples.en: Oligopolistic pricing can keep margins high even when demand falls.
examples.cn: 即使需求下降，寡头定价也能维持较高利润率。

examples.en: Regulators described the fuel retail sector as highly oligopolistic.
examples.cn: 监管者称燃油零售业高度寡头化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「oligopoly（寡头）+ istic（……的）」——少数几家说了算的 → 寡头垄断的

root: oligopoly（希腊 oligos「少数」+ pōlein「卖」，仿 monopoly 于 19 世纪后期造出）+ 后缀 -ist + -ic，构成「寡头市场特征的」形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one small group: a market takes the shape of few sellers, and that shape is then read as structure, pricing, rivalry, coordination, concentration, barriers, regulatory label, and finally any field held by a few.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个小群体展开：市场呈现出少数卖方的形状，这个形状再被读作结构、定价、竞争、协同、集中度、壁垒、监管标签，最后是任何由少数把持的领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four pieces left on a board, each watching the others.
core.cn: 核心意象：棋盘上只剩四枚棋子，彼此盯着对方。

branches.en: SHAPE AND PRICE: the few-seller form, and the prices it produces.
branches.cn: 形态与价格：少数卖方的形态，以及它所产生的价格。

branches.en: RIVALRY AND COORDINATION: moves answered move by move, and the quiet alignment that can follow.
branches.cn: 竞争与协同：一步被一步回应，以及随后可能出现的安静一致。

branches.en: CONCENTRATION: the top few hold most of the market.
branches.cn: 集中度：前几家握住大部分市场。

branches.en: BARRIERS AND LABEL: newcomers blocked by cost, and the word regulators put on the sector.
branches.cn: 壁垒与标签：新来者被成本挡住，以及监管者贴在该行业上的词。

branches.en: ANY SMALL CIRCLE: four studios, four clubs, any field held by a handful.
branches.cn: 任何小圈子：四家制片厂、四家俱乐部，任何被少数把持的领域。

intro.en: The adjective piles an English suffix complex onto a Greek-style compound, so the compound and the ending can be read separately.
intro.cn: 这个形容词在一个希腊式复合词上叠了英语后缀组合，因此复合词与词尾可以分开读。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base word here; the pattern of -isticus came through French from Greek -istikos, while oligos and pōlein remain Greek.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁基础词；-isticus 的模式经法语来自希腊 -istikos，而 oligos 与 pōlein 仍是希腊语。

items.example: The element also appears in oligarchy.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分也出现在 oligarchy 中。

items.example: The selling element stays unchanged across the family.
items.exampleCN: 「卖」这个成分在整个词族中保持不变。

items.example: The industry became an oligopoly.
items.exampleCN: 该行业成了寡头市场。

items.example: Each oligopolist matched the rival's cut.
items.exampleCN: 每个寡头都跟随对手降价。

items.example: The market remains oligopolistic.
items.exampleCN: 该市场仍呈寡头格局。

items.example: The three firms priced oligopolistically.
items.exampleCN: 这三家企业以寡头方式定价。

items.example: The duopolistic route raised fares together.
items.exampleCN: 这条双寡头航线一起提价。

items.example: Monopolistic conduct drew a fine.
items.exampleCN: 垄断行为招致罚款。

items.example: The club had an oligarchic board.
items.exampleCN: 俱乐部有一个寡头式董事会。

items.example: The industry is highly concentrated.
items.exampleCN: 该产业高度集中。

definition_en: the set of laws and enforcement measures that keep markets competitive
core_image: 审查室里，审查员把几份合并申请摊开，用红笔在市场份额一栏画圈
scene: 审查室里，工作人员把几份合并申请摊在桌上，在市场份额一栏画了红圈。Competition policy blocked the merger because it would have left three firms controlling most of the market.
sceneCN: 这里 competition policy 指「维护市场竞争的法律与执法体系」（第 1 个义项：反垄断与竞争规制的政策整体）；句意为竞争政策阻止了这桩合并，因为它会让三家企业在市场的大半份额上说了算。图中可辨识物件：合并申请文件、红笔圈注、市场份额表、审查室文件柜。

pos.zh: 竞争政策（不可数；指不同国家或不同领域的政策体系时可作可数）

forms.label: 复数（不同国家或领域的政策）
相关名词（竞争主管机构）

senses.title: The whole body of competition law
senses.titleCN: 竞争法律与执法的整体
senses.definition: the statutes, authorities and remedies that together protect competition
senses.definitionCN: 共同保护竞争的法律、主管机构与救济手段的总和
senses.example: Competition policy in the region rests on one statute and one authority.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的竞争政策依赖一部法规和一个主管机构。
senses.why: policy means a chosen course of action, so the phrase names a whole programme rather than a single rule.
senses.whyCN: policy 意为选定的一套行动方针，因此这个短语指整个方案，而非单条规则。

senses.title: Merger control
senses.definition: the review of mergers and takeovers for their effect on competition
senses.definitionCN: 审查合并与收购对竞争的影响
senses.example: Competition policy stopped the takeover at the notification stage.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争政策在申报阶段就叫停了这桩收购。
senses.why: merger review is the most visible arm of competition policy because a single deal can change a market overnight.
senses.whyCN: 合并审查是竞争政策最显眼的一支，因为一笔交易可以一夜之间改变市场。

senses.title: Rules against cartels and abuse of dominance
senses.titleCN: 规制卡特尔与滥用支配地位
senses.definition: the prohibition of price-fixing agreements and of exclusionary conduct by dominant firms
senses.definitionCN: 禁止固定价格协议以及支配性企业的排他行为
senses.example: Competition policy fined the carriers for dividing routes.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争政策对划分航线的航空公司处以罚款。
senses.why: the oldest targets of competition law are agreements among rivals and conduct that forecloses entry.
senses.whyCN: 竞争法最古老的规制对象就是对手之间的协议与封闭市场的排他行为。

senses.title: Control of state aid and subsidies
senses.definition: the rules limiting government support that distorts competition
senses.definitionCN: 限制政府支持造成竞争扭曲的规则
senses.example: Competition policy required the region to recover the illegal grant.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争政策要求该地区追回这笔非法补助。
senses.why: a subsidy can favour one firm as effectively as a private agreement, so the policy reaches into public budgets.
senses.whyCN: 补贴能像私人协议一样有效地偏袒某家企业，因此这项政策伸进公共预算。

senses.title: Market opening and liberalization
senses.definition: measures that remove legal barriers and let new suppliers enter
senses.definitionCN: 取消法律壁垒、允许新供应商进入的措施
senses.example: Competition policy opened the rail network to new operators.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争政策把铁路网络向新运营商开放。
senses.why: in formerly state-run sectors, the first task is to create rivals rather than to police them.
senses.whyCN: 在原先由国家经营的行业里，首要任务是把对手造出来，而非看管它们。

senses.title: Competition advocacy
senses.definition: work that persuades other agencies and the public to protect competition
senses.definitionCN: 说服其他机构与公众保护竞争的工作
senses.example: The authority's competition policy includes advocacy before local councils.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构的竞争政策包括在地方议会前进行倡导。
senses.why: many barriers are created by other regulators, so competition bodies must argue their case outside their own courtroom.
senses.whyCN: 许多壁垒由其他监管者造成，因此竞争机构必须在本部门法庭之外陈述理由。

senses.title: Cross-border coordination
senses.definition: cooperation among jurisdictions on mergers and conduct that cross borders
senses.definitionCN: 不同法域就跨境合并与行为进行的合作
senses.example: Competition policy now includes joint review of global deals.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争政策如今包括对全球交易的联合审查。
senses.why: a deal filed in one capital can affect buyers in another, so national policies need common procedures.
senses.whyCN: 在一个首都申报的交易可能影响另一国的买主，因此各国政策需要共同程序。

senses.title: Any policy that keeps markets orderly
senses.titleCN: 任何维护市场秩序的政策组合
senses.definition: the wider set of rules that shape how firms may compete, including consumer and sector rules
senses.definitionCN: 塑造企业可如何竞争的更广规则，包括消费者与行业规则
senses.example: Some scholars treat consumer protection as part of competition policy.
senses.exampleCN: 一些学者把消费者保护视为竞争政策的一部分。
senses.why: the boundary of the phrase is disputed because many rules affect the same market outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语的边界有争议，因为许多规则影响同一个市场结果。

intro.en: Competition comes from Latin competere 'to strive together'. Policy comes through Old French policie from Latin politia, itself from Greek politeia 'citizenship, constitution', from polis 'city'. The phrase is twentieth-century public language. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: competition 来自拉丁 competere「一起力争」。policy 经古法语 policie 上溯拉丁 politia，再上溯希腊 politeia「公民身份、政体」，其根为 polis「城邦」。整个短语是 20 世纪公共用语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Polis meant 'city, city-state'. It is the root behind politics, policy, police and polity, though each word took a different route into English.
items.cn: polis 意为「城邦、城市」。它是 politics、policy、police 与 polity 的共同根源，但每个词进入英语的路径不同。

items.en: Politeia meant the condition of being a citizen, and so the constitution or administration of a city.
items.cn: politeia 指公民身份的状况，因此也指城邦的政体或治理。

items.en: Latin politia rendered the Greek noun as 'government, administration', losing the sense of citizenship.
items.cn: 拉丁 politia 把希腊名词译为「政府、行政」，失去了「公民身份」一层。

items.en: Old French policie meant organized government; English borrowed it first in that sense, then narrowed it to a chosen plan of action.
items.cn: 古法语 policie 指有组织的治理；英语先以此义借入，后收窄为选定的行动方案。

items.en: The phrase became standard in the twentieth century with the growth of antitrust enforcement; early statutes such as the Sherman Act of 1890 supplied its tools.
items.cn: 随着反垄断执法的发展，这个短语在 20 世纪成为标准说法；1890 年《谢尔曼法》等早期法规提供了其工具。

items.en: The exact first printed use of the full phrase is not recorded; mid twentieth-century legal and economic writing supplies the earliest examples.
items.cn: 完整短语的最早印刷用例没有确切记录；20 世纪中期的法律与经济写作提供最早例子。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek root polis that are constantly confused with policy; group two holds near terms for the rules that protect competition.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊词根 polis、常与 policy 混淆的词；第二组是保护竞争的相关规则的说法。

entries.definition: From politia through French, but it came to mean the force that keeps public order, not a plan of action.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语出自 politia，却转指维持公共秩序的警力，而非行动方案。

entries.definition: From Greek politika 'affairs of the city', the activity of governing; policy is a chosen course within that activity.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 politika「城邦事务」，指治理活动；policy 是该活动内选定的路线。

entries.definition: An organized political community; it names the body, while policy names what the body decides.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的政治共同体；它指这个实体，而 policy 指该实体所决定的事。

entries.definition: The rivalry that the policy protects; competition is what the rules aim at, not the rules themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 该政策所保护的竞争；competition 是规则的目标，而非规则本身。

entries.definition: The body of law aimed at trusts and monopolies; it is the American name for much of competition policy.
entries.definitionCN: 针对托拉斯与垄断的法律体系；它是竞争政策很大一部分的美国名称。

entries.definition: Any rule issued by an authority; only the subset concerned with rivalry belongs to competition policy.
entries.definitionCN: 主管机构发布的任何规则；只有涉及竞争的那一部分属于竞争政策。

entries.definition: The removal of state controls to let private suppliers enter; it is one instrument of competition policy.
entries.definitionCN: 取消国家控制以让私人供应商进入；它是竞争政策的一种工具。

entries.definition: Continuous monitoring of market conduct; competition policy adds enforcement powers that supervision may lack.
entries.definitionCN: 对市场行为的持续监控；竞争政策另加强制执行权，而监督未必具备。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: competition + policy: the rules that keep rivalry alive.
normal.cn: competition + policy：让竞争活下去的规则。

normal.en: The family runs compete, competition, competitive, competitor, competition policy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 compete、competition、competitive、competitor、competition policy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the legal sense: competition policy enforcement, competition policy authority, competition policy review.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出法律义：竞争政策执法、竞争政策主管机构、竞争政策审查。

normal.en: The phrase has four usual tools: merger control, cartel rules, dominance rules and state-aid control.
normal.cn: 这个短语通常有四种工具：合并审查、卡特尔规则、支配地位规则与国家援助控制。

normal.en: policy came from the word for a city, so it names a chosen course for a community.
normal.cn: policy 出自「城邦」一词，因此它指一个共同体选定的路线。

abstract.en: Picture a referee who can stop a merger of two teams before the season starts.
abstract.cn: 想象一名裁判在赛季开始前就能叫停两支队伍的合并。

abstract.en: Picture a red circle drawn around one number on a share table.
abstract.cn: 想象在份额表上的一个数字周围画了红圈。

abstract.en: Picture a rulebook that applies to the players and to the league office alike.
abstract.cn: 想象一本规则手册，对球员和联盟办公室同样适用。

examples.en: Competition policy prevented the two largest chains from merging.
examples.cn: 竞争政策阻止了两家最大连锁企业合并。

examples.en: Effective competition policy needs independence from the ministry it regulates.
examples.cn: 有效的竞争政策需要独立于它所监管的部门。

examples.en: The study compared competition policy across four small economies.
examples.cn: 该研究比较了四个小型经济体的竞争政策。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「competition（竞争）+ policy（政策）」——为保住竞争而定的一整套规矩 → 竞争政策

root: competition 来自拉丁 competere「一起力争」（com- + petere「寻求」）；policy 经古法语 policie 上溯拉丁 politia，再上溯希腊 politeia「政体、公民身份」，其根为 polis「城邦」。整个短语为 20 世纪公共用语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one aim: rivalry is kept alive by rules, and those rules are then seen as a whole body of law, merger review, conduct rules, state-aid control, market opening, advocacy, cross-border work, and finally any rule that shapes a market.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个目标展开：用规则让竞争活下去，这些规则再被看作整套法律、合并审查、行为规则、国家援助控制、市场开放、倡导、跨境工作，最后是任何塑造市场的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a referee with a red pen circling one share figure before a merger is approved.
core.cn: 核心意象：一名裁判在批准合并前，用红笔圈住一个份额数字。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: statutes, authorities and remedies taken together.
branches.cn: 整体：法规、主管机构与救济手段的总和。

branches.en: BEFORE THE DEAL: merger review stops a change of ownership before it happens.
branches.cn: 交易之前：合并审查在所有权变更发生前就叫停。

branches.en: AGREEMENTS AND SUBSIDIES: private collusion and public support are treated as parallel distortions.
branches.cn: 协议与补贴：私人合谋与公共支持被视为并行的扭曲。

branches.en: MAKING RIVALS AND ARGUING: opening a sector, then persuading others to keep it open.
branches.cn: 造出对手并陈述理由：先开放行业，再说服他人保持开放。

branches.en: BEYOND ONE STATE: joint review across borders, and the disputed edge where consumer rules join in.
branches.cn: 越出一国：跨境联合审查，以及消费者规则并入的争议边界。

intro.en: The phrase pairs a Latin verb of striving with a Greek-derived noun of civic order, so each half carries a different word family.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁「力争」动词与希腊来源的「城邦秩序」名词配在一起，两半各自带着不同的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin competere supplies compete, competition and competitor; Greek polis, through politeia and Latin politia, supplies policy, politics, police and polity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 competere 提供 compete、competition 与 competitor；希腊 polis 经 politeia 与拉丁 politia 提供 policy、politics、police 与 polity。

items.example: The root underlies several words about government.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根支撑着若干关于治理的词。

items.meaning: the condition of a citizen; a constitution
items.example: The Greek noun named the order of a city.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊名词指城邦的秩序。

items.example: Latin narrowed the word toward administration.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个词收窄到行政。

items.structure: Old French policie, from Latin politia
items.example: The board adopted a new pricing policy.
items.exampleCN: 董事会通过了新的定价政策。

items.example: Politics decides who writes the rules.
items.exampleCN: 政治决定由谁来写规则。

items.meaning: the force that keeps public order
items.example: The police closed the road.
items.exampleCN: 警方封闭了这条路。

items.example: The polity has three levels of government.
items.exampleCN: 这个政治共同体有三层政府。

items.example: Suppliers compete on delivery time.
items.exampleCN: 供应商在交货时间上竞争。

items.example: Competition keeps prices low.
items.exampleCN: 竞争使价格保持低位。

items.example: Antitrust suits followed the merger.
items.exampleCN: 合并之后随之而来的是反垄断诉讼。

definition_zh: 定价；定价工作；价格体系
definition_en: the activity or system of setting prices for goods and services
core_image: 一张价目表被反复改写，铅笔字迹一层盖着一层，旁边的成本单也在变
scene: 商店后仓里，经理在价目表上来回改动，成本单摊在手边，铅笔痕迹叠了好几层。Transparent pricing reduced complaints at the counter.
sceneCN: 这里 pricing 指「为商品设定价格的做法与体系」（第 1 个义项：定价这一活动本身）；句意为透明的定价减少了柜台前的投诉。图中可辨识物件：反复改写的价目表、成本单、铅笔、后仓货架。

pos.zh: 定价；定价工作（不可数）；也可作定语，如定价策略、定价模式

senses.title: The work of setting prices
senses.definition: the ongoing activity of deciding what to charge for goods or services
senses.definitionCN: 决定商品或服务收多少钱的持续活动
senses.example: Pricing takes more time than the sales staff expect.
senses.exampleCN: 定价所花的时间比销售人员预想的多。
senses.why: the -ing form names the activity itself, not any single price that results from it.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式指活动本身，而非由此产生的某一个价格。

senses.title: A firm's price system
senses.definition: the schedule of charges a seller applies across its products
senses.definitionCN: 卖方在其全部商品上采用的价格表
senses.example: Its pricing is simple: one rate for every size.
senses.exampleCN: 它的价格体系很简单：所有规格一个价。
senses.why: pricing can stand for the whole schedule because what is set is a system, not one number.
senses.whyCN: pricing 可以指整张价格表，因为被设定的是体系，而非单一数字。

senses.title: A pricing decision
senses.definition: a specific choice about what to charge, often made at a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 关于收多少钱的具体选择，常在会议上作出
senses.example: The pricing decision was postponed until the cost report arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 定价决策被推迟到成本报告送达之后。
senses.why: business writing uses the gerund attributively for discrete decisions within the activity.
senses.whyCN: 商业写作把这个动名词作定语，指该活动中的一项项具体决策。

senses.title: A method of arriving at a price
senses.definition: the procedure used to calculate a price, such as cost-plus or value-based
senses.definitionCN: 计算价格所用的程序，如成本加成或价值导向
senses.example: Cost-based pricing ignores what buyers are willing to pay.
senses.exampleCN: 成本导向定价忽略买主愿意付多少。
senses.why: the word shifts from the act to the method once analysts compare approaches.
senses.whyCN: 当分析者比较不同做法时，这个词就从动作转向方法。

senses.title: The level at which prices sit
senses.definition: the general height of charges relative to cost or to rivals
senses.definitionCN: 收费相对于成本或对手的总体高度
senses.example: Premium pricing kept the brand's margins high for years.
senses.exampleCN: 溢价定价让这个品牌的利润率多年保持高位。
senses.why: the gerund can name a level as well as an act when the question is how high prices are.
senses.whyCN: 当问题落在价格有多高时，这个动名词也可以指水平，而不只是动作。

senses.title: Dynamic and algorithmic pricing
senses.definition: setting prices by rules or software that change with demand and stock
senses.definitionCN: 由随需求与库存变动的规则或软件来设定价格
senses.example: Airline pricing changes every few minutes as seats sell.
senses.exampleCN: 随着座位售出，航空定价每隔几分钟就变一次。
senses.why: software made price changes continuous, so the activity became a running process rather than an annual decision.
senses.whyCN: 软件使改价连续进行，因此这项活动成了持续过程，而非年度决策。

senses.title: Transfer pricing inside a group
senses.definition: the setting of internal charges between units of the same company
senses.definitionCN: 同一公司各单位之间设定内部收费
senses.example: Transfer pricing rules decide how much profit each country may tax.
senses.exampleCN: 转移定价规则决定每个国家可以征多少利润税。
senses.why: internal prices do not face a market, so the term became a technical branch with its own rules.
senses.whyCN: 内部价格不面对市场，因此这个词成了一个有独立规则的技术分支。

senses.title: Valuing anything scarce
senses.titleCN: 对任何稀缺物的估值（抽象义）
senses.definition: the act of putting a value on time, risk or access rather than on goods
senses.definitionCN: 为时间、风险或准入而非商品标出价值的行为
senses.example: The clinic's pricing of appointments reflects how long each slot is held.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所对预约的定价反映了每个时段被占用多久。
senses.why: once anything can be allocated, the word can price it, even without a shelf.
senses.whyCN: 一旦任何东西可以被分配，即使没有货架，这个词也能为其定价。

intro.en: Pricing is English price plus the gerund suffix -ing. Price came through Old French pris from Latin pretium 'price, value, reward'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pricing 是英语 price 加动名词后缀 -ing 构成。price 经古法语 pris 上溯拉丁 pretium「价格、价值、报酬」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pretium meant 'price, value, reward'. It is also the source of precious and of the verb appraise, both through the idea of worth.
items.cn: pretium 意为「价格、价值、报酬」。它也是 precious 与动词 appraise 的来源，二者都经「价值」这一概念。

items.en: Old French pris carried the Latin noun into the sense of a stated charge for goods.
items.cn: 古法语 pris 把拉丁名词带入「对商品标出的价钱」这一意义。

items.en: English borrowed price in the thirteenth century, first for the amount asked in a sale and soon for value in general.
items.cn: 英语在 13 世纪借入 price，先指买卖中索要的金额，很快也指一般价值。

items.en: The native suffix -ing formed nouns of action, as in selling and building; pricing is the regular action noun of the verb price.
items.cn: 本族后缀 -ing 构成动作名词，如 selling、building；pricing 是动词 price 的规则动作名词。

items.en: Pricing became a named business function in the twentieth century, when firms separated it from accounting and sales.
items.cn: 20 世纪，企业把定价从会计与销售中分出，pricing 才成为一项有名称的职能。

items.en: The exact first use of pricing as a business term is not recorded; the word form itself is regular and fully documented.
items.cn: pricing 作为商业术语的最早用例没有确切记录；词形本身是规则构成，且有完整书证。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the price family plus two words that look similar but descend differently; group two holds near terms for the work of fixing a charge.
note.cn: 第一组是 price 词族中的词形，外加两个形似但来源不同的词；第二组是表示「确定收费」的近义说法。

entries.definition: The charge itself or the act of setting it; pricing is the ongoing activity or system built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指收费本身或标价动作；pricing 是建立其上的持续活动或体系。

entries.definition: The participle, used for goods that have already been given a price, as in a priced catalogue.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，用于已经标好价的商品，如标价目录。

entries.definition: In the sense of value, prize is a variant of price; in the sense of an award, it comes from French prendre 'to take', a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 在「价值」义上，prize 是 price 的变体；在「奖赏」义上，它来自法语 prendre「拿取」，词根不同。

entries.definition: From ad- plus pretiare 'to value', so it means to assess worth; it is a relative, not a misspelling of apprise.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ad- 加 pretiare「估价」，意为评估价值；它是同源词，并非 apprise 的错误拼写。

entries.definition: The work of calculating what a product costs to make; pricing starts from cost but also considers demand.
entries.definitionCN: 计算产品制造成本的工作；定价从成本出发，但也考虑需求。

entries.definition: An estimate of the worth of an asset; pricing a product is a narrower commercial case.
entries.definitionCN: 对资产价值的估算；给产品定价是更窄的商业情形。

entries.definition: A price stated for a specific job or order; it is one output of pricing, not the system.
entries.definitionCN: 针对某项工作或订单报出的价格；它是定价的一项产出，而非体系。

entries.definition: Fixing tariffs, often by a regulator for utilities; it is pricing under external control.
entries.definitionCN: 确定费率，常由监管者为公用事业设定；它是受外部控制的定价。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: price + -ing: the activity of putting a charge on goods.
normal.cn: price + -ing：给商品标出价钱的活动。

normal.en: The family runs price, priced, pricey, priceless, overprice, underprice.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 price、priced、pricey、priceless、overprice、underprice。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the business sense: pricing strategy, pricing policy, pricing model.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出商业义：定价策略、定价政策、定价模型。

normal.en: Three common methods are cost-based, value-based and competitor-based.
normal.cn: 三种常见方法是成本导向、价值导向与对手导向。

normal.en: Software made dynamic pricing possible, so prices now move by the minute.
normal.cn: 软件使动态定价成为可能，价格如今按分钟变动。

abstract.en: Picture a price list rewritten until the pencil marks pile up.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价目表被改了又改，铅笔痕迹叠成一层。

abstract.en: Picture a tag that is turned over and over in a shopper's hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签在顾客手里被翻来覆去。

abstract.en: Picture a clock and a price tag wired to the same dial.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟和一张价签接在同一个表盘上。

examples.en: Pricing is now handled by a team that meets every Monday.
examples.cn: 定价如今由一个每周一开会的团队负责。

examples.en: The company changed its pricing after losing a third of its customers.
examples.cn: 公司在流失三分之一顾客后改变了定价。

examples.en: Transfer pricing rules decide where a multinational's profit is taxed.
examples.cn: 转移定价规则决定跨国企业的利润在哪里纳税。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「price（价格）+ ing（正在做）」——正在给商品定价格 → 定价

root: price 经古法语 pris 上溯拉丁 pretium「价格、价值、报酬」；pricing 为 price 加本族动名词后缀 -ing，指定价活动或价格体系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of numbering: a seller decides what to charge, and that decision is then seen as an activity, a system, a discrete decision, a method, a level, a running algorithm, an internal transfer, and finally a value put on anything scarce.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个「标数」动作展开：卖方决定收多少，这个决定再被看作活动、体系、单项决策、方法、水平、持续运行的算法、内部转移，最后是为任何稀缺物标出的价值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a price list rewritten so often that the pencil marks layer over one another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张价目表被改得太频繁，铅笔痕迹层层叠起。

branches.en: ACT AND DECISION: the ongoing work, and one choice made inside it.
branches.cn: 活动与决策：持续进行的工作，以及其中的一项选择。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM: a whole schedule of charges taken as one arrangement.
branches.cn: 体系：把整张收费表当作一个安排。

branches.en: METHOD AND HEIGHT: how the number is reached, and how high it sits.
branches.cn: 方法与高度：数字如何算出，以及它处在多高。

branches.en: MACHINE AND GROUP: prices that move by the minute, and charges inside one company.
branches.cn: 机器与集团：按分钟变动的价格，以及一家公司内部的收费。

branches.en: ANYTHING SCARCE: the same act applied to time, risk or access.
branches.cn: 任何稀缺物：同一动作被用于时间、风险或准入。

intro.en: Pricing is a native action noun built on a Latin-derived noun, so one half is a borrowed root and the other a native suffix.
intro.cn: pricing 是建在拉丁来源名词上的本族动作名词，一半是借来的词根，另一半是本族后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin pretium supplies price, precious and appraise; English -ing supplies pricing, selling and building.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pretium 提供 price、precious 与 appraise；英语 -ing 提供 pricing、selling 与 building。

items.example: The Latin noun underlies several English words of worth.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词支撑着若干表示价值的英语词。

items.structure: Latin pretium via Old French pris
items.example: The price rose with the tariff.
items.exampleCN: 价格随关税上升。

items.example: Pricing is reviewed each quarter.
items.exampleCN: 定价每季度审查一次。

items.example: Every item in the window is priced.
items.exampleCN: 橱窗里每件商品都标了价。

items.example: The repair was pricey but quick.
items.exampleCN: 这次修理很贵，但很快。

items.example: The letters are priceless to the family.
items.exampleCN: 这些信对这个家庭而言无价。

items.example: The launch was overpriced and stalled.
items.exampleCN: 首发定价过高，卖不动。

items.example: They underpriced the service to win users.
items.exampleCN: 他们把服务定价过低以争取用户。

items.example: An expert appraised the house.
items.exampleCN: 一位专家为这栋房子估了价。

items.example: The metal is precious but common in the trade.
items.exampleCN: 这种金属很珍贵，但在业内很常见。

latinEntries.meaning: to value, set a price on

definition_en: the amount of money for which something is sold, or what must be given up to obtain something
core_image: 货架上一枚小小的价签，数字不大，却决定了谁会拿起这件商品
scene: 货架前，顾客翻过价签看背面，又把商品放回原位，转身走向更便宜的一排。The price of the coat was reduced twice before it sold.
sceneCN: 这里 price 指「商品的售价」（第 1 个义项：出售商品所要求的金额）；句意为这件外套的价格降了两次才卖出去。图中可辨识物件：货架价签、翻看标签的顾客、更便宜的一排商品、被放回的外套。

pos.zh: 给…定价；标价（动词重音不变）

senses.title: The money asked for a good
senses.definition: the amount of money a seller asks for an item or service
senses.definitionCN: 卖方为某件商品或服务索要的金额
senses.example: The price of the coat was reduced twice before it sold.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套的价格降了两次才卖出去。
senses.why: the core sense is a stated amount, which is what a price tag shows.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一个被标出的金额，也就是价签所显示的内容。

senses.title: What must be given up
senses.titleCN: 为得到某物必须付出的代价
senses.definition: the cost in effort, risk or lost alternatives of obtaining something
senses.definitionCN: 为获得某物而在努力、风险或放弃的其他选择上付出的代价
senses.example: The price of success was three years without weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 成功的代价是三年没有周末。
senses.why: the word extends from money to any scarce thing given up, because both are what one pays.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从金钱延伸到任何被放弃的稀缺之物，因为两者都是所付出的东西。

senses.title: To set a price on something
senses.definition: to decide and mark the amount to be charged for an item
senses.definitionCN: 决定并标出某项商品的收费金额
senses.example: They priced the tickets at twenty pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把票价定为二十英镑。
senses.why: the verb is the noun turned into an act of assigning the amount.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词转为「指派金额」的动作。

senses.title: The general level of prices
senses.definition: the average level of charges across an economy at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期一个经济体中收费的平均水平
senses.example: Prices rose faster than wages for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 有十年时间，物价涨得比工资快。
senses.why: in the plural the word often means the general level rather than one tag.
senses.whyCN: 用复数时，这个词常指总体水平，而非一张价签。

senses.title: A reward offered for a capture
senses.titleCN: 为缉拿或寻回而设的赏金
senses.definition: a sum offered to anyone who finds a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 向找到某人或某物者提供的金额
senses.example: A price was put on the fugitive's head.
senses.exampleCN: 有人为这名逃犯的人头设了赏金。
senses.why: the older sense treats a reward as the amount paid for a result.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的义项把赏金看作「为某个结果所付的金额」。

senses.title: A quoted buying or selling rate
senses.definition: the rate at which a dealer will buy or sell in a financial market
senses.definitionCN: 交易商在金融市场愿意买进或卖出的价位
senses.example: The bond price fell after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 公告之后债券价格下跌。
senses.why: financial markets quote two prices, a bid and an offer, so the noun names a rate rather than a tag.
senses.whyCN: 金融市场报出买价与卖价两个价位，因此这个名词指一个比率，而非标签。

senses.title: Odds in racing or betting
senses.definition: the odds offered on a horse or outcome, expressed as a price
senses.definitionCN: 对某匹马或某个结果开出的赔率，以价位表示
senses.example: The bookmaker shortened the price on the favourite.
senses.exampleCN: 博彩商调低了热门马匹的赔率。
senses.why: betting calls odds a price because the stake buys a chance at a return.
senses.whyCN: 博彩把赔率称作 price，因为赌注买到的是一次回报机会。

senses.title: Any scale of worth
senses.titleCN: 衡量与交换的价值尺度（抽象义）
senses.definition: the measure by which a society or person values something
senses.definitionCN: 社会或个人用来衡量某物价值的尺度
senses.example: Health has no price in the ordinary market sense.
senses.exampleCN: 健康在普通市场意义上没有价格。
senses.why: the word generalizes once value itself is what is being measured, not only goods.
senses.whyCN: 当被衡量的是价值本身而非仅商品时，这个词就一般化了。

intro.en: Price comes through Old French pris from Latin pretium 'price, value, reward'. It is a doublet of prize in the sense of value, but not of prize meaning an award. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: price 经古法语 pris 上溯拉丁 pretium「价格、价值、报酬」。它与表示「价值」的 prize 是对偶词，但与表示「奖赏」的 prize 不是。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pretium covered price, value and reward, so the Latin word already contained both the commercial and the figurative seeds.
items.cn: pretium 兼指价格、价值与报酬，因此这个拉丁词已同时含商业义与比喻义的种子。

items.en: Old French pris meant the amount asked or the worth of a thing, and passed both senses to English.
items.cn: 古法语 pris 指索要的金额或某物的价值，并把这两层意思都传给英语。

items.en: English price appears in the thirteenth century; the plural came to mean the general cost of living.
items.cn: 英语 price 出现于 13 世纪；其复数后来指一般生活成本。

items.en: Prize meaning value is a variant of price; prize meaning an award came from Old French prise 'a capture', from prendre 'to take', a different root.
items.cn: 表示「价值」的 prize 是 price 的变体；表示「奖赏」的 prize 来自古法语 prise「捕获」，再上溯 prendre「拿取」，词根不同。

items.en: The figurative price of success and the betting price of a horse extend the same core: something must be paid for an outcome.
items.cn: 「成功的代价」与赛马的「赔率」都延伸同一核心：为了某个结果必须付出某物。

items.en: The exact first English citation is approximate. Latin pretium and Old French pris are well documented.
items.cn: 最早的英语书证年代只是约数。拉丁 pretium 与古法语 pris 都有充分书证。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like price or share its root but differ in sense; group two holds near terms for an amount charged.
note.cn: 第一组是形似 price 或与其同根、但意义不同的词；第二组是表示「所收金额」的近义词。

entries.definition: As value, it is a doublet of price; as an award, it descends from prendre 'to take'. Only the first sense is etymologically the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 作「价值」解时，它是 price 的对偶词；作「奖赏」解时，上溯 prendre「拿取」。只有前一义在词源上是同一个词。

entries.definition: From Latin pretiosus 'costly', built on pretium; it describes worth, not the amount charged.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 pretiosus「贵重」，建于 pretium 之上；它描述价值，而非所收金额。

entries.definition: From ad- plus pretiare 'to value'; it means to estimate worth, not to set a selling price.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ad- 加 pretiare「估价」；意为估算价值，而非设定售价。

entries.definition: Built on price with -y, meaning expensive; it describes the level, not the amount itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 price 加 -y 构成，意为昂贵；它描述水平，而非金额本身。

entries.definition: The expense of making or obtaining something; price is what the buyer pays, and the two need not be equal.
entries.definitionCN: 制作或取得某物的支出；price 是买主所付，两者不必相等。

entries.definition: The amount a provider demands for a service; it is close to price but more common for services and fees.
entries.definitionCN: 服务提供者索要的金额；与 price 接近，但更常用于服务与费用。

entries.definition: A fixed payment for a professional service or privilege; it is a kind of price with a narrower setting.
entries.definitionCN: 为专业服务或特权支付的固定款项；它是范围更窄的一类价格。

entries.definition: The worth of something to a person; price is what is asked, while value is what is judged.
entries.definitionCN: 某物对某人的价值；price 是所要之数，value 是被判断的价值。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin pretium 'value': the same root runs through price, precious and appraise.
normal.cn: 拉丁 pretium「价值」：同一词根贯穿 price、precious 与 appraise。

normal.en: The family runs price, pricing, priced, pricey, priceless, overprice, underprice.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 price、pricing、priced、pricey、priceless、overprice、underprice。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the commercial sense: market price, price tag, price increase.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出商业义：市场价格、价签、价格上涨。

normal.en: The figurative sense is marked by of: the price of success, the price of silence.
normal.cn: 比喻义由 of 标出：成功的代价、沉默的代价。

normal.en: Betting uses price for odds, because a stake buys a chance at a return.
normal.cn: 博彩用 price 指赔率，因为赌注买到的是一次回报机会。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny tag that decides whether a hand reaches out or moves on.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚小小的价签，决定一只手是伸出去还是走开。

abstract.en: Picture a coin placed on one side of a scale and a thing on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象天平一边放硬币，另一边放物品。

abstract.en: Picture a finish line with a toll booth in front of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条终点线前面立着一个收费亭。

examples.en: The price of the ticket includes the ferry crossing.
examples.cn: 票价包含渡船费用。

examples.en: They paid a high price for ignoring the warning.
examples.cn: 他们因忽视警告付出了高昂代价。

examples.en: The dealer quoted a price for the old car.
examples.cn: 经销商为这辆旧车报了价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「price（价格）」——货架上那个决定买不买的数字 → 价格、代价

root: 拉丁 pretium「价格、价值、报酬」→ 古法语 pris → 英语 price；与表示「奖赏」的 prize 不同源，但与表示「价值」的 prize 属对偶词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one number: a seller states what a thing costs, and that number is then read as a tag, a sacrifice, a verb, a general level, a reward, a quoted rate, betting odds, and finally any scale of worth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个数字展开：卖方说出某物要多少钱，这个数字再被读作价签、牺牲、动词、总体水平、赏金、报价、赔率，最后是任何价值尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one small tag whose number decides whether a hand reaches out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚小价签，其数字决定一只手是否伸出。

branches.en: AMOUNT AND ACT: the number on the tag, and the act of putting it there.
branches.cn: 金额与动作：价签上的数字，以及把数字放上去的动作。

branches.en: SACRIFICE AND SCALE: what must be given up, and the wider measure of worth it implies.
branches.cn: 牺牲与尺度：必须放弃的东西，以及它所含的更广价值尺度。

branches.en: THE GENERAL LEVEL: prices in the plural become the cost of living.
branches.cn: 总体水平：复数的 prices 成为生活成本。

branches.en: REWARD AND QUOTE: a sum offered for a capture, and a rate quoted in a market.
branches.cn: 赏金与报价：为缉拿所设的金额，以及市场中报出的价位。

branches.en: BETTING ODDS: the stake buys a chance, so the odds are called a price.
branches.cn: 博彩赔率：赌注买到机会，因此赔率被称作价格。

intro.en: Price is a borrowed Latin noun that English has turned into a verb, an adjective and an action noun, so the family spreads in several directions.
intro.cn: price 是借入的拉丁名词，英语把它变成动词、形容词与动作名词，因此词族向多个方向展开。

latinIntro.en: Latin pretium, pretiosus and pretiare supply price, precious, appraise and appreciate; English suffixes supply pricing, priced, pricey and priceless.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pretium、pretiosus 与 pretiare 提供 price、precious、appraise 与 appreciate；英语后缀提供 pricing、priced、pricey 与 priceless。

items.example: The root carries both money and worth.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根兼含金钱与价值。
