items.example: The price held steady all year.
items.exampleCN: 价格全年保持稳定。

items.example: Prices fell in the autumn.
items.exampleCN: 物价在秋季下降。

items.example: The book is priced at twelve pounds.
items.exampleCN: 这本书标价十二英镑。

items.example: Pricing is handled centrally.
items.exampleCN: 定价由总部统一处理。

items.example: The seats were pricey but comfortable.
items.exampleCN: 座位很贵，但很舒适。

items.example: The diary is priceless to historians.
items.exampleCN: 这本日记对历史学者而言无价。

items.example: The seller overpriced the flat.
items.exampleCN: 卖方把这套房子定价过高。

items.example: They underpriced the tickets and sold out.
items.exampleCN: 他们把票价定得过低，结果售罄。

items.example: A valuer appraised the painting.
items.exampleCN: 一位估价师为这幅画估了价。

latinEntries.meaning: to value, set a price on

definition_en: a planned approach to setting prices in order to reach a commercial goal
core_image: 一张白板上画着两条价格曲线，一条先高后低，一条先低后高，旁边写着目标
scene: 会议室白板上画着两条价格曲线，一条从高处下滑，一条从低处爬升，中间标着同一款产品。The firm switched to a penetration pricing strategy to win shelf space.
sceneCN: 这里 pricing strategy 指「有计划的定价方针」（第 1 个义项：为达成商业目标而设计的定价总体方案）；句意为这家企业改用渗透定价策略来争取货架位置。图中可辨识物件：白板上的两条价格曲线、目标标注、同一款产品的图片、会议室座椅。

senses.title: An overall plan for setting prices
senses.definition: a deliberate plan for how a firm will set and change prices over time
senses.definitionCN: 企业如何设定并随时调整价格的有意规划
senses.example: The pricing strategy targets value rather than volume.
senses.exampleCN: 这项定价策略瞄准价值而非销量。
senses.why: strategy is a plan of action, so the phrase is the plan behind the prices rather than any single price.
senses.whyCN: strategy 是行动方案，因此这个短语指价格背后的方案，而非某一个价格。

senses.title: Skimming the market
senses.definition: charging a high initial price and lowering it as early buyers are exhausted
senses.definitionCN: 先定高价，待早期买主被吸收后再逐步降价
senses.example: The skimming pricing strategy paid for development in the first year.
senses.exampleCN: 撇脂定价策略在第一年就收回了开发成本。
senses.why: the image is cream skimmed from the top of milk, taking the richest layer first.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻是把牛奶表面最富的一层先撇走，即先取最肥的利润。

senses.title: Penetration pricing
senses.definition: setting a low initial price to win share quickly and raise it later
senses.definitionCN: 先以低价迅速争取份额，之后再提价
senses.example: A penetration pricing strategy won the platform a million users.
senses.exampleCN: 渗透定价策略为该平台赢得了一百万用户。
senses.why: the low price is meant to penetrate a market already occupied by rivals.
senses.whyCN: 低价意在渗入已被对手占据的市场。

senses.title: Value-based pricing
senses.definition: setting prices from what buyers judge the product to be worth
senses.definitionCN: 根据买主对产品价值的判断来定价
senses.example: Value-based pricing strategy raised margins without raising costs.
senses.exampleCN: 价值导向定价策略在不提高成本的情况下提高了利润率。
senses.why: the starting point is the buyer's valuation, not the seller's cost.
senses.whyCN: 起点是买主的估值，而不是卖方的成本。

senses.title: Cost-plus pricing
senses.definition: adding a standard margin to the measured cost of production
senses.definitionCN: 在测得的成本上加上标准利润率
senses.example: A cost-plus pricing strategy is safe but slow to respond.
senses.exampleCN: 成本加成定价策略稳妥，但反应慢。
senses.why: the plan begins with cost and adds a fixed percentage, so it is a rule rather than a judgement.
senses.whyCN: 该方案以成本为起点加上固定百分比，因此是规则而非判断。

senses.title: Dynamic and price-discriminating
senses.definition: changing prices by segment, time or demand to capture more of each buyer's willingness to pay
senses.definitionCN: 按群体、时间或需求改价，以更多地取得每位买主的支付意愿
senses.example: The airline's pricing strategy charges business travellers more than holiday makers.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司的定价策略对商务旅客收取比度假者更高的价格。
senses.why: the plan treats each segment as a separate market with its own acceptable price.
senses.whyCN: 该方案把每个细分群体当作有各自可接受价格的独立市场。

senses.title: Psychological pricing
senses.definition: setting prices to shape how buyers perceive the number rather than to reflect cost
senses.definitionCN: 为影响买主对数字的感知而定价，而非反映成本
senses.example: A psychological pricing strategy ended every tag in nine.
senses.exampleCN: 心理定价策略让每张价签都以九结尾。
senses.why: the plan works on perception, so the last digit matters as much as the total.
senses.whyCN: 该方案作用于感知，因此末位数字与总额同样重要。

senses.title: A plan for any exchange
senses.titleCN: 为任何交换设定的条件（抽象义）
senses.definition: the terms on which a party will exchange something, applied beyond retail
senses.definitionCN: 一方交换某物所依的条件，越出零售场景
senses.example: The museum's pricing strategy for school visits is a single flat fee.
senses.exampleCN: 这家博物馆对学校参观的定价策略是统一一口价。
senses.why: once price is any value scale, a strategy for price is a plan for any exchange.
senses.whyCN: 一旦价格泛指任何价值尺度，定价策略就是任何交换的方案。

intro.en: Pricing is English price plus -ing, and price goes back to Latin pretium 'value'. Strategy comes from Greek stratēgia 'generalship', from stratos 'army' and agein 'to lead'. The phrase is twentieth-century business language. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: pricing 是英语 price 加 -ing，price 上溯拉丁 pretium「价值」。strategy 来自希腊 stratēgia「将帅之术」，由 stratos「军队」与 agein「引领」构成。整个短语是 20 世纪商业用语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stratos meant 'army, host'. The same element appears in stratagem and in the military title strategos.
items.cn: stratos 意为「军队、队伍」。同一成分出现在 stratagem 与军职 strategos 中。

items.en: Agein meant 'to lead, drive'. Joined to stratos it produced the sense of leading an army.
items.cn: agein 意为「引领、驱动」。与 stratos 结合后产生「统领军队」之义。

items.en: Stratēgia meant 'generalship, command', and by extension the art of planning a campaign.
items.cn: stratēgia 意为「将帅之职、统帅」，引申为筹划战役的技艺。

items.en: Stratēgēma meant a trick or device used in war, the source of English stratagem; it is a relative, not a synonym of strategy.
items.cn: stratēgēma 指战争中的计谋或手段，是英语 stratagem 的来源；它与 strategy 同族，但并非同义词。

items.en: Strategy entered English as a military term, and only in the twentieth century moved into business planning.
items.cn: strategy 作为军事术语进入英语，到 20 世纪才转入商业规划。

items.en: The exact first use of the full phrase is not recorded; it belongs to twentieth-century marketing writing. Every Greek element is attested.
items.cn: 完整短语的最早用例没有确切记录，属 20 世纪营销写作。每个希腊成分都有书证。

note.en: Group one holds words from the strategy family that are confused with strategy or share only a look; group two holds near terms for a pricing plan.
note.cn: 第一组是 strategy 词族中易混的词，或仅形似的词；第二组是表示定价方案的近义说法。

entries.definition: From Greek stratēgēma, a device or trick used to gain an advantage; it is one move inside a strategy.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 stratēgēma，指为取得优势而用的手段或计谋；它是战略中的一招。

entries.definition: Relating to strategy; a pricing strategy is the noun, while strategic describes its level.
entries.definitionCN: 与战略相关的；pricing strategy 是名词，strategic 描述其层次。

entries.definition: From Latin sternere 'to spread', meaning a layer; it looks like strategy but shares no root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 sternere「铺开」，意为「层」；形似 strategy，却无共同词根。

entries.definition: The work of setting prices; a pricing strategy is the plan that guides that work.
entries.definitionCN: 设定价格的工作；定价策略是指导这项工作的方案。

entries.definition: A simple word for the same idea, used for published tariffs such as phone plans.
entries.definitionCN: 同一意思的朴素说法，常用于电话套餐等公开费率。

entries.definition: A rule set by management or a regulator; it is broader and less market-specific than a strategy.
entries.definitionCN: 由管理层或监管者设定的规则；比策略更宽，也更少针对具体市场。

entries.definition: A formula for deriving prices; the model is a tool used inside the strategy.
entries.definitionCN: 推算价格的公式；模型是策略内部使用的工具。

entries.definition: A single short-term action such as a temporary discount; a strategy is the longer plan it serves.
entries.definitionCN: 如临时折扣等单次短期动作；策略是它所服务的更长方案。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: pricing + strategy: a plan for the numbers on the tags.
normal.cn: pricing + strategy：为价签上的数字所定的方案。

normal.en: The family runs price, pricing, strategy, strategic, strategically, strategist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 price、pricing、strategy、strategic、strategically、strategist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the common plans: skimming, penetration, value-based, cost-plus.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出常见方案：撇脂、渗透、价值导向、成本加成。

normal.en: strategy comes from the Greek word for leading an army, so it is a plan for a campaign.
normal.cn: strategy 出自希腊语「统领军队」，因此它是战役层面的方案。

normal.en: A stratagem is one trick inside the plan, not the plan itself.
normal.cn: stratagem 是方案中的一计，而非方案本身。

abstract.en: Picture two curves on one whiteboard, one falling and one climbing.
abstract.cn: 想象同一块白板上的两条曲线，一条下降，一条上升。

abstract.en: Picture a general's map and a shop's price list pinned side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象将军的地图与商店的价目表并排钉在墙上。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag with an arrow drawn through it, pointing down.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签上画着向下的箭头。

examples.en: The board reviewed its pricing strategy after the merger.
examples.cn: 合并之后，董事会重新审视了定价策略。

examples.en: A penetration pricing strategy can buy share but may train buyers to expect discounts.
examples.cn: 渗透定价策略可以换得份额，却可能让买主习惯折扣。

examples.en: Their pricing strategy treats each region as a separate market.
examples.cn: 他们的定价策略把每个地区当作独立市场。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pricing（定价）+ strategy（战略）」——为价格打仗的总体计划 → 定价策略

root: pricing 为 price 加 -ing，price 上溯拉丁 pretium「价值」；strategy 来自希腊 stratēgia「将帅之术」（stratos「军队」+ agein「引领」）。整个短语为 20 世纪商业用语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one plan: a firm chooses how its prices will move, and that plan is then seen as an overall course, skimming, penetration, value pricing, cost-plus, dynamic pricing, psychological pricing, and finally a plan for any exchange.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个方案展开：企业选择价格如何变动，这个方案再被看作总体方针、撇脂、渗透、价值定价、成本加成、动态定价、心理定价，最后是任何交换的方案。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two price curves drawn on one whiteboard, one falling and one rising.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一块白板上画着两条价格曲线，一条下降，一条上升。

branches.en: THE OVERALL PLAN: the deliberate course behind every individual tag.
branches.cn: 总体方案：每一张价签背后有意选定的路线。

branches.en: TWO OPENINGS: start high and skim, or start low and penetrate.
branches.cn: 两种开局：先高后撇脂，或先低后渗透。

branches.en: TWO ANCHORS: begin from the buyer's value, or begin from the seller's cost.
branches.cn: 两个锚点：从买主的价值出发，或从卖方的成本出发。

branches.en: SEGMENTS AND PERCEPTION: charge each group differently, and shape how the number is read.
branches.cn: 细分与感知：对不同群体收不同价，并塑造数字被如何读取。

branches.en: BEYOND RETAIL: the same plan applied to school visits or any exchange.
branches.cn: 越出零售：同一方案被用于学校参观或任何交换。

intro.en: The phrase joins an English action noun from Latin pretium to a Greek noun of command, so it mixes two word families.
intro.cn: 这个短语把建在拉丁 pretium 上的英语动作名词，与希腊「统帅」名词组合，混用了两个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin pretium gives price and pricing; Greek stratos and agein give strategy, strategic, strategist and stratagem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pretium 提供 price 与 pricing；希腊 stratos 与 agein 提供 strategy、strategic、strategist 与 stratagem。

definition_zh: 折扣；减价；打折；贴现；低估
definition_en: a reduction from the usual price, or to reduce or dismiss the importance of something
core_image: 橱窗上贴着一张斜线划掉旧价的纸签，新数字用红笔写在一旁
scene: 橱窗玻璃上贴着一张划掉旧价的纸签，红笔在旁边写下更低的数字。The shop offered a discount to clear the winter stock before spring.
sceneCN: 这里 discount 指「从原价中减去的折扣」（第 1 个义项：卖方在原价基础上让出的金额）；句意为这家店打折以在春季前清掉冬装库存。图中可辨识物件：划掉旧价的纸签、红笔新价、橱窗玻璃、冬装货架。

pos.zh: 打折出售；贴现；低估；不予考虑（动词重音后移）

senses.title: A reduction from the usual price
senses.definition: an amount taken off the normal price of a good or service
senses.definitionCN: 从商品或服务的正常价格中减去的金额
senses.example: The shop offered a discount to clear the winter stock.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店打折以清掉冬装库存。
senses.why: dis- 'apart' plus count 'reckon' gives 'count off', and the sum counted off is the reduction.
senses.whyCN: dis-「分开」加 count「计算」构成「减掉」，被减掉的那部分就是折扣。

senses.title: The rate of reduction
senses.definition: the percentage or fraction by which a price is lowered
senses.definitionCN: 价格被降低的百分比或比例
senses.example: A discount of twenty per cent applied to all coats.
senses.exampleCN: 所有外套一律打八折。
senses.why: the noun can measure the cut rather than the sum, so discounts are often stated as rates.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词可以计量削减的比例而非金额，因此折扣常以比率表示。

senses.title: To sell at a reduced price
senses.definition: to offer goods for less than the usual price
senses.definitionCN: 以低于通常价格出售商品
senses.example: They discounted the last few pairs to make space.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把最后几双打折出售以腾出空间。
senses.why: the verb is the noun turned into an act of applying the reduction.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词转为「施加削减」的动作。

senses.title: To discount a future sum
senses.definition: to calculate the present value of a payment due later
senses.definitionCN: 计算一笔日后付款的现值
senses.example: The bank discounted the bill at a lower rate.
senses.exampleCN: 银行以较低的贴现率买下了这张票据。
senses.why: the financial sense counts off the interest that would accrue before payment, so it is the same 'count off'.
senses.whyCN: 金融义减掉的是付款前会累积的利息，因此仍是同一个「减掉」。

senses.title: To dismiss something as unimportant
senses.titleCN: 认为不重要而不予考虑
senses.definition: to treat a claim, risk or report as less significant than it appears
senses.definitionCN: 把某种说法、风险或报告看得没有表面上那么重要
senses.example: Officials discounted the rumour until the second report appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 官员们一直不把传言当回事，直到第二份报告出现。
senses.why: to count something off is to leave it out of the reckoning, and from there it means to disregard.
senses.whyCN: 把某物从计算中减掉，就是把它排除在考量之外，由此引申为不予采信。

senses.title: To deduct in advance
senses.definition: to take an amount off a payment before it is made
senses.definitionCN: 在付款之前先从金额中扣掉一部分
senses.example: The fee is discounted from the first month's salary.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔费用从第一个月工资中扣除。
senses.why: the accounting sense keeps the literal image of subtracting before the total is handed over.
senses.whyCN: 会计义保留「在交出总额之前先减去」的字面意象。

senses.title: A discounted bill of exchange
senses.definition: a bill bought below its face value before it falls due
senses.definitionCN: 在到期前以低于面值的价格买入的汇票
senses.example: The trader lived on discounted bills rather than cash.
senses.exampleCN: 这名商人靠贴现票据而非现金周转。
senses.why: the instrument is named by the operation performed on it, a common pattern in trade finance.
senses.whyCN: 这种票据以施加于其上的操作命名，这是贸易金融中的常见模式。

senses.title: To take a statement at reduced value
senses.titleCN: 削弱某种说法的分量（抽象义）
senses.definition: to accept a claim only with reservations, as if its value were marked down
senses.definitionCN: 只带保留地接受某种说法，仿佛其价值被打了折
senses.example: Take his estimate at a discount; he always rounds up.
senses.exampleCN: 他的估计要打个折扣听，他总是往上取整。
senses.why: the price image survives as a metaphor: a claim, like a bill, can be worth less than its face value.
senses.whyCN: 价格意象作为比喻留存：一种说法如同票据，可能不值其面值。

intro.en: Discount is dis- 'apart, away' plus count, from Old French conter, from Latin computare 'to reckon', built on com- and putare 'to reckon, prune'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: discount 是 dis-「分开、去掉」加 count；count 经古法语 conter 上溯拉丁 computare「计算」，由 com- 与 putare「计算、修剪」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Putare meant 'to reckon, consider, prune'. The pruning image explains why the same verb also gives amputate and why computing is a cutting-down of possibilities.
items.cn: putare 意为「计算、考虑、修剪」。修剪的意象解释了同一动词为何也衍生 amputate，以及为何计算像是把可能性削减下来。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus putare produced computare 'to reckon together, calculate', the source of compute, count and account.
items.cn: com-「共同」加 putare 构成 computare「合起来算、计算」，是 compute、count 与 account 的来源。

items.en: Old French conter carried the verb into English as count, first for reckoning and then for numbering items.
items.cn: 古法语 conter 把这个动词带入英语作 count，先指核算，后指数数。

items.en: The Latin prefix dis- adds 'apart, away', so discount literally means to count something off a total.
items.cn: 拉丁前缀 dis- 增添「分开、去掉」，因此 discount 字面上是把某物从总数中减掉。

items.en: The financial sense of discounting a bill appears in the sixteenth century; the retail sense of cutting a price became common in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 对票据贴现的金融义出现在 16 世纪；削减售价的零售义到 19 世纪才普遍。

items.en: The exact first English citation is approximate. The Latin and French steps are documented, and no part of the word is invented.
items.cn: 最早的英语书证年代只是约数。拉丁与法语环节有书证，词中没有编造成分。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same counting family that differ in direction or prefix; group two holds near terms for a price cut.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「计算」词族、但方向或前缀不同的词；第二组是表示降价的近义说法。

entries.definition: To reckon or number; discount adds the prefix that means counting something off.
entries.definitionCN: 计算或数数；discount 加上表示「减掉」的前缀。

entries.definition: From computare, to calculate; it shares the root but not the prefix, so it carries no sense of a reduction.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 computare，意为计算；共享词根但不带该前缀，因此不含削减之义。

entries.definition: From the same counting verb, a record of sums; an account may show a discount but is not one.
entries.definitionCN: 同出该计算动词，指账目记录；账目可以显示折扣，但它本身不是折扣。

entries.definition: With re- it means either to count again or to tell in detail; neither sense is a price reduction.
entries.definitionCN: 加 re- 后或指重新计数，或指详细叙述；两义都不是降价。

entries.definition: Any lowering of an amount or price; it is broader than discount and need not be a deliberate sales offer.
entries.definitionCN: 任何金额或价格的降低；比 discount 更宽，也未必是有意的促销。

entries.definition: A sum paid back after the purchase rather than taken off at the till.
entries.definitionCN: 购买之后退回的款项，而非在收银台当场减掉。

entries.definition: A price lowered on the ticket, typical of clearance stock; it is a retail form of discount.
entries.definitionCN: 价签上被调低的价钱，常见于清仓商品；它是折扣的一种零售形式。

entries.definition: An amount subtracted from a payment or income, often for tax or costs; it is not a sales offer.
entries.definitionCN: 从付款或收入中减去的金额，常用于税务或成本；它不是促销让价。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: dis- 'apart' + count 'reckon': to count an amount off the total.
normal.cn: dis-「分开」+ count「计算」：从总数中减掉一笔。

normal.en: The family runs count, compute, account, recount, discount, discounted.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 count、compute、account、recount、discount、discounted。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the retail sense: offer a discount, at a discount, discount store.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出零售义：提供折扣、以折扣价、折扣店。

normal.en: The finance sense is marked by a rate: the discount rate, a discounted bill.
normal.cn: 金融义由「率」标出：贴现率、贴现票据。

normal.en: The dismissive sense is marked by its object: discount a rumour, discount a warning.
normal.cn: 轻视义由宾语标出：不采信传言、不重视警告。

abstract.en: Picture a tag with a line through the old number and a smaller one beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签，旧数字被划掉，旁边写着更小的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a coin counted off a pile and put aside.
abstract.cn: 想象从一堆硬币中数出一枚放到旁边。

abstract.en: Picture a document whose face value is crossed out before it is traded.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文件在交易前面值被划掉。

examples.en: The bookshop gave students a ten per cent discount.
examples.cn: 书店给学生打九折。

examples.en: Analysts discount the survey because the sample was small.
examples.cn: 分析者不采信这项调查，因为样本太小。

examples.en: The bank discounted the bill three weeks before it fell due.
examples.cn: 银行在票据到期前三周买下了它。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「dis（去掉）+ count（数）」——从总价里数掉一部分 → 折扣

root: dis-「分开、去掉」+ count（经古法语 conter 上溯拉丁 computare「计算」，com- + putare「计算、修剪」）；字面义为「从总数中减掉」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one subtraction: an amount is counted off, and that subtraction is then applied to a price, a rate, a sale, a future payment, a claim's credibility, a wage payment, a traded bill, and finally to any statement taken at less than face value.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个减法展开：一笔数目被减掉，这个减法再依次用于价格、比率、出售、未来付款、说法的可信度、工资付款、交易票据，最后是任何按低于面值采信的说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tag whose old number is struck through and replaced by a smaller one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张价签，旧数字被划掉，换成更小的数字。

branches.en: AMOUNT AND RATE: the sum taken off, and the percentage that expresses it.
branches.cn: 金额与比率：被减掉的金额，以及表达它的百分比。

branches.en: THE SALE: the act of applying the reduction to goods.
branches.cn: 出售：把削减施加于商品的动作。

branches.en: FINANCE: a future payment valued today, and a bill bought below face value.
branches.cn: 金融：把未来付款折算成今天价值，以及低于面值买入的票据。

branches.en: DISMISS AND DEDUCT: counting a claim out of the reckoning, and taking money off a payment.
branches.cn: 轻视与扣除：把某种说法排除在考量之外，以及从付款中减钱。

branches.en: AT LESS THAN FACE VALUE: any statement heard with a reservation.
branches.cn: 低于面值：任何带保留听取的说法。

intro.en: Discount is a prefixed verb whose base is a borrowed Latin verb of reckoning, so dis-, count and the Latin root each carry part of the meaning.
intro.cn: discount 是带前缀的动词，其基干是借入的拉丁「计算」动词，因此 dis-、count 与拉丁词根各自承担一部分意义。

latinIntro.en: Latin computare supplies count, compute, account and recount; dis- supplies the sense of taking away.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 computare 提供 count、compute、account 与 recount；dis- 提供「去掉」之义。

items.example: The prefix turns counting into counting off.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「计算」变成「减掉」。

items.structure: Old French conter, from Latin computare
items.example: Count the change before you leave.
items.exampleCN: 离开前把零钱数清。

items.example: The program computes the total.
items.exampleCN: 程序算出总额。

items.example: The account shows every payment.
items.exampleCN: 账目列出了每笔付款。

items.example: They recounted the votes twice.
items.exampleCN: 他们把票数了两次。

items.meaning: to count off; a price cut
items.example: The shop discounted the last pairs.
items.exampleCN: 这家店把最后几双打折出售。

items.meaning: sold or valued below the usual figure
items.example: Discounted stock sold within a week.
items.exampleCN: 打折库存在一周内售完。

items.meaning: the practice of valuing future sums today
items.meaningCN: 把未来金额折算为今日价值的做法
items.example: Discounting future income is standard practice.
items.exampleCN: 对未来收入折现是标准做法。

items.example: The discounter undercut every local rival.
items.exampleCN: 这家折扣店压过了所有本地对手。

items.example: Undiscounted tickets cost twice as much.
items.exampleCN: 未打折的票要贵一倍。
